description: Comma-separated list of alternative or equivalent part numbers that can substitute for this component. Supports flexible sourcing and reduces downtime when primary part is unavailable.

The category of asset to which this RFID tag is attached. Container is most common for waste management operations. Equipment includes compactors, balers, and scales. Vehicle tags are used for non-fleet tracking (fleet has separate DOT-compliant systems).
The date when this RFID tag was assigned to a specific asset (container, equipment, or other trackable item). Marks the beginning of the tag-asset relationship for tracking and billing purposes.

The manufacturer batch or lot number for this RFID tag. Used for quality control, recall management, and performance analysis by production batch. If a batch shows high failure rates, all tags from that batch can be identified and replaced proactively.
The date and time when this RFID tag record was first created in the system. Used for audit trails and data lineage tracking.

Indicates whether the RFID tag uses encrypted communication protocols. True for tags with built-in encryption capabilities. Encryption enhances security for sensitive applications and prevents unauthorized tag cloning.

The IP (Ingress Protection) rating indicating the tags resistance to dust and water. Waste container RFID tags typically require IP67 or higher for outdoor exposure, pressure washing, and harsh environmental conditions.

The unique EPC identifier encoded in the RFID tag, typically a 96-bit or 128-bit hexadecimal value conforming to GS1 EPC standards. This is the actual data read from the tag during scanning operations.

The manufacturer-specified expected operational lifespan of the RFID tag in years under normal operating conditions. Passive tags typically last 10-20 years; active tags with batteries last 3-7 years. Used for replacement forecasting and total cost of ownership calculations.

The radio frequency band on which the tag operates. UHF (860-960 MHz) is standard for waste container tracking due to long read range and fast read rates. Frequency band determines reader compatibility and regulatory compliance.
The date when the RFID tag was physically installed or affixed to the asset. May differ from assignment_date if the tag was pre-assigned before physical installation.

Describes where on the asset the RFID tag is physically mounted (e.g., front panel, lid interior, side wall, handle). Important for troubleshooting read failures and ensuring consistent tag placement across the fleet.
The date and time when this RFID tag record was most recently updated. Used for change tracking and data synchronization across systems.
The geographic latitude coordinate where the RFID tag was last successfully read. Captured from GPS-enabled mobile readers on collection vehicles or fixed readers at facilities.
The geographic longitude coordinate where the RFID tag was last successfully read. Used in conjunction with latitude for geospatial analysis and container location tracking.

Identifier of the RFID reader device that performed the last successful read. May be a vehicle-mounted reader, handheld scanner, or fixed portal reader. Used for reader performance analysis and troubleshooting.

reference: Infor EAM Condition Assessment; ISO 55000 Asset Management

description: Binary or conditional outcome of the inspection: pass (asset meets all criteria), fail (asset does not meet criteria and cannot be used), or conditional_pass (asset can be used with restrictions or minor repairs).
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910; DOT FMCSA Inspection Standards

reference: Infor EAM Document Management; ISO 55000 Asset Management

description: Timestamp when this inspection record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail and data lineage.

Boolean indicator (True/False) specifying whether this inspection was performed to satisfy a regulatory requirement from EPA, OSHA, DOT, or local enforcement agencies. Used for audit trail and compliance reporting.
reference: EPA RCRA; OSHA 29 CFR 1910; DOT FMCSA; Enviance EHS Compliance Tracking

description: Reference number or citation for the specific regulatory requirement that mandated this inspection, such as EPA permit condition, OSHA standard section, or DOT inspection code. Supports audit documentation.
reference: EPA RCRA; OSHA 29 CFR 1910; DOT FMCSA; Enviance EHS

description: Boolean indicator (True/False) specifying whether a safety incident or near-miss occurred during the inspection. Triggers incident reporting workflow in Enviance EHS.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1904; Enviance EHS Incident Management

description: Weather conditions at the time of inspection (e.g., clear, rain, snow, extreme heat), relevant for outdoor asset inspections where environmental factors may affect inspection quality or asset condition assessment.

Reference to the fixed asset whose condition is being tracked. Links to the asset master record in SAP PM or Infor EAM.
Reference to the work order under which this condition assessment was performed. Links to Infor EAM or SAP PM work order records.

Indicates whether this assessment was performed to satisfy regulatory compliance requirements (EPA, OSHA, DOT, state environmental agencies).
Explanation or root cause for the change in asset condition. Captures factors such as wear and tear, environmental exposure, accident damage, or maintenance improvements.
Numeric condition score on a standardized scale (typically 0-100) representing asset health. Enables quantitative trend analysis and predictive maintenance modeling.
Date and time when this condition history record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.
Indicates whether any critical or safety-related defects were identified during this assessment. Triggers immediate corrective action workflows.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the estimated repair cost. Supports multi-currency financial reporting.
The new condition rating assigned during this assessment. Used for asset health monitoring and replacement prioritization.
Number of defects or issues identified during this condition assessment. Quantifies asset health problems for prioritization and trend analysis.
Number of supporting documents (inspection reports, test results, certifications) attached to this condition assessment.
Assessment of environmental risk posed by the asset in its current condition. Critical for landfill liners, leachate systems, and hazardous waste containers.
Estimated number of years the asset can continue to operate in its current condition before replacement is required. Supports capital planning and budgeting.
Estimated cost to repair or remediate the identified condition issues. Supports maintenance budgeting and repair-versus-replace analysis.
Latitude coordinate where the condition assessment was performed. Supports field inspection verification and mobile workforce tracking.
Longitude coordinate where the condition assessment was performed. Supports field inspection verification and mobile workforce tracking.
External reference number or document identifier for the inspection report or assessment record. Supports traceability to source documentation.
Full name of the technician or inspector who recorded the condition change. Provides human-readable reference for audit and accountability.

Scheduled date for the next condition assessment based on inspection frequency requirements and asset criticality. Drives preventive maintenance scheduling.
Assessment of how the current asset condition affects operational performance and service delivery. Supports asset replacement prioritization.
Number of photos or images attached to this condition assessment record. Supports visual documentation of asset condition.

Unique identifier for the GPS telemetry record. Primary key for time-series GPS position and telemetry data from GPS-equipped stationary assets and containers.
Foreign key reference to the asset being tracked. Links to the asset master record for the container, roll-off, portable compactor, or other GPS-equipped stationary asset.
Estimated accuracy radius of the GPS position reading in meters. Represents the confidence interval within which the true position lies. Lower values indicate higher precision.
Elevation above sea level in meters at the time of GPS reading. Used for terrain analysis and asset placement verification in landfill cells or hilly terrain.
Remaining battery charge level of the GPS device as a percentage (0.00 to 100.00). Used for proactive device maintenance and battery replacement scheduling.
Date and time when this telemetry record was first inserted into the data platform. System-generated audit field in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
Unique identifier of the GPS tracking device hardware unit. Used to identify the specific GPS tracker installed on the asset, distinct from the asset itself.
reference: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) and GPS Device Registry

description: Operational status of the GPS tracking device. Active = functioning normally, Inactive = powered off or not transmitting, Maintenance = undergoing service, Fault = malfunction detected, Decommissioned = removed from service.
Date and time when the GPS position and telemetry data was captured by the device. Represents the real-world observation time in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
Version number of the GPS device firmware at the time of transmission. Used for device management, compatibility tracking, and firmware update planning.
Current status of the asset relative to its assigned geofence zone. Inside = within authorized zone, Outside = beyond authorized zone, Entering = crossing into zone, Exiting = crossing out of zone.
Foreign key reference to the geofence zone the asset is currently within. Null if asset is outside all defined geofences. Used for authorized location verification and breach detection.
Measure of GPS position accuracy. Lower values indicate better precision. <1 = Ideal, 1-2 = Excellent, 2-5 = Good, 5-10 = Moderate, 10-20 = Fair, >20 = Poor.
Compass direction of asset movement in degrees (0-360). 0/360 = North, 90 = East, 180 = South, 270 = West. Null if asset is stationary.
Date when the GPS device was installed on the asset. Used for device age tracking, warranty management, and replacement planning.
Date when the GPS device last underwent maintenance, battery replacement, or firmware update. Used for preventive maintenance scheduling and device lifecycle tracking.
Geographic latitude coordinate of the asset position in decimal degrees. Range: -90.0000000 to +90.0000000. Positive values represent North, negative values represent South.
Geographic longitude coordinate of the asset position in decimal degrees. Range: -180.0000000 to +180.0000000. Positive values represent East, negative values represent West.
Boolean indicator of whether unauthorized movement was detected for a stationary asset. True = unexpected movement detected, False = asset stationary or movement authorized. Used for theft detection.

Communication network used to transmit the telemetry data. Cellular = 3G/4G/5G mobile network, Satellite = satellite communication, WiFi = wireless local area network, LoRa = long-range low-power network.
Free-text field for additional comments, observations, or context about the telemetry reading. Used for documenting anomalies, investigation findings, or special circumstances.
Number of GPS satellites the device was connected to at the time of reading. Higher count indicates better position accuracy. Minimum 3 required for 2D fix, 4 for 3D fix.

Quality of the GPS satellite signal at the time of reading. Excellent = 4+ satellites with strong signal, Good = 3-4 satellites, Fair = 2-3 satellites, Poor = 1-2 satellites, No Signal = 0 satellites.
Instantaneous speed of the asset in kilometers per hour. For stationary assets, non-zero values indicate unauthorized movement or theft. Used for tamper detection and movement alerts.
Boolean indicator of whether the GPS device detected tampering or unauthorized removal attempt. True = tamper detected, False = no tamper. Triggers security alerts and theft investigation.
Ambient temperature reading from the GPS device sensor in degrees Celsius. Used for device health monitoring and environmental condition tracking. Null if device does not have temperature sensor.

Classification of what triggered this telemetry transmission. Scheduled = routine periodic update, Event Triggered = geofence breach or movement alert, On Demand = manual query, Emergency = tamper or critical alert.
Date and time when this telemetry record was last modified in the data platform. System-generated audit field in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).

business_glossary_term: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) Read Event ID
description: Unique identifier for each RFID tag read event captured during container service operations or facility gate transactions.
Reference to the physical container (dumpster, roll-off, cart) associated with the RFID tag at the time of the read event.
Reference to the specific route stop where the RFID read occurred. Null for non-route events such as facility gate scans.
reference: AMCS Platform Route Stop Master Data

description: Reference to the customer account associated with the container at the time of the read event. Used for billing confirmation and service verification.
Reference to the driver operating the vehicle at the time of the RFID read. Null for stationary facility readers. Used for driver performance tracking and service accountability.
Reference to the facility (landfill, MRF, transfer station, maintenance shop) where the RFID read occurred. Null for mobile route-based reads.
Unique identifier encoded in the RFID tag affixed to the container. Typically a 96-bit or 128-bit EPC (Electronic Product Code) represented as hexadecimal string.
reference: ISO/IEC 15963 RFID Unique Identification, EPCglobal Tag Data Standards

description: Reference to the collection route being executed when the RFID read occurred. Null for facility gate or yard scan events.
Reference to the service address where the container was read. Used to validate that service occurred at the correct location per the service agreement.
Reference to the collection vehicle on which the RFID reader was mounted at the time of the read event. Null for stationary readers at facilities.
Identifier of the specific antenna on the reader device that captured the tag read. Multi-antenna readers use this to determine read direction and position.
Indicates whether this read event qualifies for billing confirmation based on read quality, location accuracy, and business rules. True if eligible, False if not.
Indicates whether this read event is a duplicate of a previous read within a defined time window (typically 60 seconds). True if duplicate, False if unique read.

Classification of the RFID read event indicating the business context: service confirmation during collection, yard inventory scan, facility gate entry/exit, manual handheld scan, or exception handling scan.
Code indicating any exception or anomaly detected during the read event. Empty string if no exception. Used for quality control and dispute resolution.
Human-readable description of the exception or anomaly, if any. Null if no exception occurred. Provides context for operational review and customer service.

business_glossary_term: Global Positioning System (GPS) Accuracy in Meters
description: Estimated accuracy of the GPS coordinates in meters at the time of the read. Lower values indicate higher precision. Used to assess reliability of location data for billing disputes.
reference: GPS Standard Positioning Service Performance Standard

description: Date and time when the raw RFID read event was processed and loaded into the lakehouse silver layer. Used for data lineage and latency monitoring.
Direction of vehicle or container movement at the time of read: inbound (entering facility), outbound (exiting facility), stationary (no movement), or unknown (direction not determinable).
Geographic latitude coordinate (decimal degrees) captured by GPS at the time of the RFID read. Used for service verification and geospatial analytics.
Geographic longitude coordinate (decimal degrees) captured by GPS at the time of the RFID read. Used for service verification and geospatial analytics.
Normalized quality score (0-100) calculated from signal strength, GPS accuracy, and reader diagnostics. Higher scores indicate more reliable reads suitable for billing confirmation.
Sequential number of this read within the route execution or facility session. Used to reconstruct the chronological order of service events and detect duplicate reads.
Precise date and time when the RFID tag was read by the reader device. Captured in UTC and converted to local time zone for reporting.
Unique identifier of the RFID reader device that captured the tag read. Typically mounted on collection trucks, facility gates, or yard scanners.
Version number of the firmware running on the RFID reader device at the time of the read. Used for troubleshooting and ensuring device compliance with operational standards.
Business date (local time zone) on which the service event occurred. Used for partitioning, billing cycle alignment, and operational reporting. Derived from read_timestamp.

business_glossary_term: Radio Frequency (RF) Signal Strength in Decibels-Milliwatts (dBm)
description: Received signal strength indicator (RSSI) of the RFID tag read measured in dBm. Higher values (closer to zero) indicate stronger signal. Used for read quality assessment and troubleshooting.
Unique identifier of the read event record in the source operational system. Used for traceability and reconciliation with upstream systems.
Operational system that originated the RFID read event: AMCS Platform, Geotab Fleet Telematics, Locus Dispatch, or MANUAL for handheld scanner entries.
RFID tag memory bank from which the data was read: EPC (Electronic Product Code), TID (Tag Identifier), USER (user-defined data), or RESERVED (access/kill passwords).
reference: EPCglobal Gen2 RFID Tag Memory Architecture

Unique identifier for the asset utilization measurement record.
Reference to the business unit that owns or operates the asset. Used for organizational reporting and asset portfolio analysis across divisions.
Reference to the facility where the asset is located during the measurement period. Links to landfill sites, MRF facilities, transfer stations, WTE plants, or maintenance shops.
Reference to the fixed asset being measured. Links to the asset master record in SAP PM or Infor EAM.
The unit of measure for the actual throughput value. Must be compatible with the rated capacity unit for utilization rate calculation.

The actual measured throughput or usage during the measurement period. For containers, this is average fill level. For compactors and balers, this is actual tons processed. For scales, this is actual weighing transactions completed.

The category of fixed asset being measured. Determines which utilization metrics are applicable (e.g., containers track fill level, compactors track operating hours and cycles, scales track transaction count). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: container|compactor|baler|scale|transfer_station|landfill_cell|mrf_equipment — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

Average fill level percentage for containers during the measurement period. Calculated from RFID sensor readings or visual inspection data. Used to optimize service frequency and identify oversized or undersized containers.
The cost center responsible for the asset during the measurement period. Used for financial allocation of asset utilization costs and ROI analysis. Sourced from SAP FI/CO.
The timestamp when this utilization measurement record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.

Total number of operational cycles completed during the measurement period. Applicable to compactors (compaction cycles) and balers (baling cycles). Captured from equipment control systems or manual logs.

The system or method used to capture the utilization measurement. Identifies whether data came from automated sensors (RFID, GPS), manual entry, or integrated systems (AMCS, Infor EAM, SAP PM). Critical for data quality assessment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: rfid_sensor|gps_telematics|manual_entry|amcs_platform|infor_eam|sap_pm|scale_system|equipment_controller — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Number of calendar days the asset was idle (not used or serviced) during the measurement period. Critical metric for container rationalization and redeployment decisions.

Total idle hours (non-operating time) during the measurement period. For containers, this represents days without service. For equipment, this is available hours minus operating hours. Used to identify underutilized assets for redeployment.

The method used to obtain the utilization measurement. Automated sensor indicates RFID or IoT device readings, manual inspection indicates visual assessment, system calculated indicates derived metrics from operational systems.
The end date of the utilization measurement period. Defines the conclusion of the observation window for calculating utilization metrics.
The start date of the utilization measurement period. Defines the beginning of the observation window for calculating utilization metrics.

Data quality score for the utilization measurement, ranging from 0.00 to 1.00. Higher scores indicate more reliable data. Factors include data source reliability, completeness, and timeliness. Used to weight measurements in analytics.

The precise date and time when the utilization measurement was captured or recorded. For sensor-based measurements, this is the sensor reading timestamp. For manual entries, this is the data entry timestamp.
The user ID or system account that last modified this utilization measurement record. Used for change tracking and accountability.
The timestamp when this utilization measurement record was last modified. Used for change tracking and audit trail purposes.
Free-text notes providing additional context about the utilization measurement. May include explanations for anomalies, special circumstances affecting utilization, or operational observations.
Total operating hours recorded for the asset during the measurement period. Applicable to compactors, balers, and other powered equipment. Captured from equipment hour meters or telematics systems.
Maximum fill level percentage recorded during the measurement period. Indicates whether the container size is adequate for the customer's waste generation rate.

The calculated utilization rate expressed as a percentage of rated capacity. For containers, this is average fill level percentage. For equipment, this is operating hours divided by available hours. Used for asset rationalization and redeployment decisions.

The unit of measure for the rated capacity value. Varies by asset type: cubic yards for containers, tons per day for processing equipment, transactions per day for scales, operating hours for machinery.

The maximum rated capacity of the asset during the measurement period. For containers, this is volume in cubic yards. For compactors and balers, this is throughput in tons per day (TPD). For scales, this is maximum weighing transactions per day.
Indicates whether the asset is a candidate for redeployment based on utilization metrics. True if asset is underutilized at current location and could be more effectively deployed elsewhere.

Indicates whether this utilization measurement has significant impact on asset ROI analysis. True if utilization is outside acceptable thresholds and requires management attention for redeployment or disposal decisions.
Number of times the asset was serviced during the measurement period. For containers, this is the number of pickups. For equipment, this is the number of maintenance or operational service events.
Total weight in tons processed through the asset during the measurement period. Applicable to compactors, balers, scales, and processing equipment. Sourced from weight tickets and equipment logs.

Categorical assessment of the asset's utilization level. Optimal indicates efficient use, underutilized flags candidates for redeployment, overutilized indicates need for additional capacity, idle indicates no usage, out_of_service indicates asset is unavailable.
Total number of weighing transactions processed by a scale during the measurement period. Key utilization metric for landfill scales, transfer station scales, and MRF scales.
The user ID or system account that created this utilization measurement record. Used for data lineage and accountability.

Used for manifest preparation and vehicle placarding.

Date when this waste code became effective under federal or state regulations. Used to determine applicability to historical waste streams and to track regulatory changes over time. Critical for legacy waste management and compliance audits.

Maximum number of days a generator may accumulate this waste on-site before shipping to a TSDF. Typically 90 days for large quantity generators, 180 days for small quantity generators, or 270 days with approved extension. Shorter limits (e.g., 1 day) may apply to acutely hazardous wastes.

Primary hazard characteristic that qualifies this waste as hazardous under RCRA. Ignitability (D001) covers flammable liquids and oxidizers. Corrosivity (D002) covers acids and bases. Reactivity (D003) covers unstable or explosive materials. Toxicity (D004-D043) covers materials that leach toxic constituents. Listed wastes are hazardous by definition regardless of characteristics. Multiple indicates waste exhibits more than one characteristic.
Timestamp when this waste code record was last updated. Tracks regulatory changes, data corrections, and reference updates. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

Additional operational notes, clarifications, or internal guidance for using this waste code. May include common misclassifications to avoid, industry-specific interpretations, or cross-references to related codes. Free-text field for subject matter expert annotations.

Indicates whether this waste code has known recycling or reclamation pathways that may qualify for reduced regulatory requirements under RCRA recycling exemptions. True if legitimate recycling options exist (e.g., solvent recovery, metal reclamation, fuel blending).

Specific section of 40 CFR Part 261 or state regulation that defines this waste code. Provides legal reference for compliance documentation and audit trails. Format typically follows CFR structure (e.g., 40 CFR 261.31 for F-listed wastes).

CERCLA reportable quantity in pounds. If a spill or release of this waste equals or exceeds this quantity, it must be reported to the National Response Center immediately. Values typically range from 1 lb (most hazardous) to 5,000 lbs. Null if no RQ is assigned.

Quantity threshold in kilograms below which a generator may qualify for reduced regulatory requirements. Typically 100 kg per month for hazardous waste or 1 kg per month for acutely hazardous waste. Used to determine generator category (VSQG, SQG, LQG).

Two-letter state abbreviation for state-specific waste codes. Null for federal EPA codes. Used to identify which state jurisdiction defines and enforces this code. Critical for multi-state operations to ensure compliance with local regulations.

Indicates whether this waste code is a state-specific designation beyond federal EPA requirements. True when the code is defined by state environmental regulations and may not be recognized in other states. False for federal EPA codes that apply nationwide.

Date when this waste code was or will be removed from regulatory lists. Null for active codes. Populated when EPA or state agencies delist a waste code or when state-specific codes are superseded. Historical record retention required for audit trails.

description: Specific toxic constituent measured in TCLP testing for toxicity characteristic wastes. Examples include arsenic, barium, cadmium, chromium, lead, mercury, selenium, silver, benzene, trichloroethylene. Only populated for D-code toxicity characteristic wastes (D004-D043).

business_glossary_term: Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) Regulatory Level (mg/L)

Specifies required treatment technology or concentration limits (e.g., DEACT for deactivation, IMERC for incineration, specific mg/L or mg/kg limits for TCLP constituents).

Subcategory designation for wastes with multiple treatment standards based on waste form or concentration. Used when a single waste code has different treatment requirements for wastewater versus non-wastewater forms, or for different concentration ranges.

Universal Treatment Standard concentration limits for underlying hazardous constituents. Specifies maximum allowable concentrations (in mg/L for TCLP or mg/kg total) for each constituent before the waste can be land disposed. Multiple constituents may be listed with their respective limits.

EPA or state hazardous waste code identifier. Format follows EPA classification: D-codes (D001-D043 for characteristic wastes), F-codes (F001-F039 for non-specific source wastes), K-codes (K001-K181 for specific source wastes), P-codes (P001-P205 for acutely hazardous commercial chemical products), U-codes (U001-U411 for toxic commercial chemical products). reference: EPA Recycling Traceability Requirements; AMCS Platform Route Management; SWANA MRF Standards

Reference to the quality control inspector who performed the most recent inspection on this bale. Supports inspector accountability, certification tracking, and quality audit trails. Links to Workday HCM employee records.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; SWANA MRF Quality Assurance Standards; Workday HCM

description: Reference to the baler machine that produced this bale. Supports equipment performance monitoring, preventive maintenance scheduling, and bale quality correlation with specific baler units via Infor EAM.
reference: Infor EAM Asset Lifecycle Management; SWANA MRF Equipment Standards

description: Reference to the sorting line within the MRF where the commodity was processed and separated prior to baling. Used for equipment performance tracking and throughput analysis by sort line.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; Infor EAM Asset Lifecycle

description: Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: When bales are produced from purchased recyclables (buy-back programs), traceability to originating PO enables COGS calculation, margin analysis, and cost accounting for purchased material - critical
Reference to the designated storage bay, pad, or warehouse location within the MRF where this bale is currently stored. Supports inventory management, FIFO rotation, and outbound logistics planning.
reference: SAP MM Inventory Management; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Foreign key linking to hazmat.waste_profile. Business justification: Contaminated bales exceeding commodity grade specifications and containing hazardous constituents require waste profiling before disposal or specialized treatment. Real business process: rejected bale

Date and time when this bale was allocated to a specific sales order or outbound shipment. Marks the transition from in_storage to allocated lifecycle status. Used for inventory turnover analysis and order fulfillment lead time tracking.
reference: SAP SD Sales and Distribution; Oracle Revenue Management

description: Human-readable barcode label affixed to the bale for physical identification and scanning during storage, quality inspection, and outbound shipment. Printed at time of production and scanned at each lifecycle checkpoint.
reference: GS1 Barcode Standards; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Bill of Lading number assigned to the outbound shipment carrying this bale. The BOL is the primary freight transport document required by DOT regulations. Null until bale is loaded for shipment. Enables shipment tracking and dispute resolution with commodity buyers.
reference: DOT 49 CFR Freight Documentation; UCC Article 7 Bills of Lading; SAP SD Transportation

description: Unique quality certification document number issued for this bale upon passing inspection, confirming it meets the specified commodity grade and buyer quality requirements. Required for certain commodity buyers and export shipments. Null if no formal certification was issued.
reference: ISO 9001 Quality Management; ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; Export Commodity Certification Requirements

description: Specific material subtype within the commodity category (e.g., OCC for Old Corrugated Cardboard, HDPE for High-Density Polyethylene, aluminum, steel, clear glass, mixed paper). Drives commodity-specific market pricing and buyer contract matching. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: OCC|ONP|mixed_paper|HDPE|PET|LDPE|aluminum|steel|tin|clear_glass|brown_glass|green_glass — promote to reference product]
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; EPA Recycling Commodity Definitions; SWANA MRF Standards

description: Primary commodity category of the bale. Classifies the recovered material stream for inventory management, market pricing, and EPA recycling diversion reporting. Core classification for MRF commodity recovery analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: paper|plastic|metal|glass|mixed|textile|electronics|organics — promote to reference product]
reference: EPA Recycling Program Guidelines; SWANA Commodity Classification Standards; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

description: Measured percentage of non-target or non-recyclable material (contaminants) present in the bale, expressed as a percentage of total bale weight. Determined during quality inspection. Exceeding buyer-specified contamination thresholds results in grade downgrade, price deduction, or rejection. Key MRF quality KPI.
reference: EPA Recycling Quality Guidelines; ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; Buyer Contract Specifications

description: Date and time when this bale record was first created in the system, typically at the moment of bale production completion. Serves as the audit trail creation timestamp for data lineage, Silver layer ingestion tracking, and SOX compliance recordkeeping.
reference: SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; GAAP Audit Trail Requirements; ISO 14001 Environmental Records

description: Number of days this bale has been in MRF storage since production. Tracked to manage inventory aging, prioritize FIFO shipment sequencing, and identify slow-moving commodity inventory that may be subject to quality degradation or market price risk. Updated daily.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; SAP MM Inventory Aging

description: Calculated density of the bale expressed as kilograms per cubic meter, derived from weight and physical dimensions. Indicates baler compression performance and material compaction ratio. Low density may signal baler maintenance needs or loose material feed. Used for baler performance KPI tracking.
reference: SWANA MRF Equipment Performance Standards; Infor EAM Asset Performance

description: Estimated monetary value of this bale in USD, calculated as weight in tons multiplied by the applicable commodity market price per ton. Used for MRF commodity inventory valuation, revenue forecasting, and financial reporting in SAP FI/CO. Not a final invoiced amount — actual sale price is recorded on the sales order.
reference: SAP FI/CO Financial Reporting; Oracle Revenue Management; GAAP Inventory Valuation Standards

description: Quality grade assigned to the bale based on contamination level, moisture content, and material purity. Grade A represents premium quality meeting buyer specifications; Grade B is acceptable with minor deviations; Grade C is marginal; off-spec fails buyer specs but is saleable at discount; rejected is unsaleable. Directly impacts commodity sale price.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; SWANA MRF Quality Standards; Buyer Contract Specifications

description: Physical height dimension of the bale in centimeters as measured at production. Combined with length and width for volume calculation, stacking safety assessment, and storage bay capacity planning.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; OSHA 29 CFR 1910 Storage Safety

description: Outcome of the most recent quality inspection for this bale. Pass indicates the bale meets all applicable grade and buyer specifications; fail results in rejection or rework; conditional pass indicates the bale is accepted with noted deviations that are within buyer tolerance.
reference: SWANA MRF Quality Assurance Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management; Buyer Contract Specifications

description: Date and time when the most recent quality inspection was performed on this bale. Used for inspection age tracking, pre-shipment inspection validity windows, and audit trail for quality certification documentation.
reference: SWANA MRF Quality Assurance Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Type of quality inspection performed on this bale. Production QC is conducted at time of baling; pre-shipment inspection occurs before loading; buyer-requested inspection is initiated by the commodity buyer; re-inspection follows a prior rejection or dispute. Determines inspection protocol and documentation requirements.
reference: SWANA MRF Quality Assurance Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management; Buyer Contract Specifications

description: Physical length dimension of the bale in centimeters as measured at production. Used with width and height to calculate bale volume, verify baler performance, and plan trailer loading configurations for outbound commodity shipments.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; DOT Freight Dimension Requirements

description: Current operational state of the bale within its lifecycle from production through disposition. In_storage: produced and available in MRF inventory; allocated: assigned to a sales order or shipment; shipped: loaded and departed facility; rejected: failed quality inspection and removed from saleable inventory; on_hold: pending re-inspection or buyer dispute resolution.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; SAP MM Inventory Management

description: Prevailing commodity market price per ton in USD at the time this bale was produced or allocated to a sales order. Captured for commodity inventory valuation, revenue forecasting, and market price trend analysis. Reflects spot market or contracted price depending on buyer agreement type.
reference: ISRI Commodity Pricing Index; SAP MM Material Valuation; Oracle Revenue Management

description: Measured moisture content of the bale expressed as a percentage of total bale weight. Excess moisture reduces net commodity value, increases transport weight without material value, and can cause mold or degradation in paper bales. Monitored against buyer moisture tolerance thresholds.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; Buyer Contract Specifications; SWANA MRF Quality Standards

description: Free-text field for operational notes, quality observations, or special handling instructions associated with this bale. Used by MRF operators and quality inspectors to document non-standard conditions not captured in structured fields (e.g., visible damage, unusual contamination type, buyer special instructions).

MRF operating shift during which this bale was produced. Used for shift-level productivity analysis, quality trend analysis by shift, and workforce scheduling optimization. Correlates bale quality and throughput metrics to specific shift teams.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; Workday HCM Workforce Scheduling

description: Date and time when the bale was ejected from the baler and production was completed. The principal business event timestamp for this MASTER_RESOURCE. Used for throughput calculations (Tons Per Day), shift productivity reporting, and bale age tracking for FIFO inventory management.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; EPA Recycling Throughput Reporting

description: Indicates whether this bale requires a follow-up quality inspection, typically after remediation of a failed inspection, buyer dispute, or conditional pass with noted concerns. True triggers a re-inspection workflow in the MRF quality management process.
reference: SWANA MRF Quality Assurance Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management

description: Documented reason for bale rejection when inspection_result is fail or lifecycle_status is rejected. Common reasons include excessive contamination, moisture above threshold, broken wires, incorrect commodity mix, or bale integrity failure. Required for root cause analysis and MRF process improvement. Null when bale passes inspection.
reference: SWANA MRF Quality Assurance Standards; EPA Recycling Program Guidelines

description: RFID tag identifier embedded in or attached to the bale for automated tracking through MRF storage, loading dock, and outbound logistics. Enables real-time inventory visibility without manual scanning. Null if facility does not use RFID.
reference: GS1 RFID Standards (EPC Gen2); AMCS Platform Container Tracking

description: Date and time when this bale was loaded onto an outbound transport vehicle and departed the MRF facility. Marks the transition to shipped lifecycle status. Used for inventory reconciliation, Bill of Lading (BOL) documentation, and commodity revenue recognition timing.
reference: SAP SD Shipping and Transportation; DOT Freight Documentation; GAAP Revenue Recognition (ASC 606)

description: Date and time when this bale record was most recently modified. Tracks lifecycle status changes, quality inspection updates, allocation events, and shipment confirmations. Used for incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer and audit compliance.
reference: SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; Databricks Delta Lake Change Data Capture; ISO 14001 Environmental Records

description: Gross weight of the bale in kilograms as measured by the baler scale or floor scale at time of production. The principal quantitative measurement for this resource. Used for Tons Per Day (TPD) throughput calculations, commodity inventory valuation, sales order fulfillment, and EPA recycling tonnage reporting.
reference: EPA Recycling Tonnage Reporting; NIST Handbook 44 Weighing Standards; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Physical width dimension of the bale in centimeters as measured at production. Combined with length and height for volume calculation, storage space planning, and trailer load optimization.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; DOT Freight Dimension Requirements

description: Number of wire ties or strapping bands securing the bale. Standard bale configurations use 4, 5, or 6 wires depending on commodity type and baler model. Deviations from standard wire count may indicate bale integrity risk during transport and are flagged during quality inspection.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; ISRI Bale Specification Guidelines

description: Unique identifier for the bale inspection record. Primary key for the bale inspection transaction.
Reference to the bale being inspected. Links to the bale production record in the Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) system.
Reference to the commodity buyer for whom this inspection was performed. Populated for buyer-requested inspections or pre-shipment inspections for specific customers.
Reference to the commodity sales order associated with this inspection. Links inspection to outbound commodity sales transaction.
Reference to the equipment used for inspection measurements (e.g., moisture meter, scale). Links to asset management for calibration tracking.
Reference to the MRF facility where the inspection occurred. Links to facility master data.
Reference to the prior inspection record for this bale. Populated for reinspections to track inspection history and corrective action effectiveness.
Reference to the employee who performed the inspection. Links to workforce/employee master data.
Measured weight of the bale in pounds at time of inspection. Used to verify production weight and calculate commodity value.
Indicates whether the bale is approved for shipment to buyer based on inspection results. True when inspection passes and all quality criteria are met.
Certificate number issued for bales that pass inspection and meet buyer specifications. Used for traceability and buyer dispute resolution.
Industry or regulatory standard against which the bale was inspected (e.g., ISRI specifications, buyer-specific requirements, EPA guidelines). Supports regulatory reporting and buyer certification.
Measured percentage of non-target materials or contaminants in the bale. Critical metric for commodity grade determination and buyer acceptance. Expressed as percentage (0.00 to 100.00).
reference: Institute of Scrap Recycling Industries (ISRI) Specifications

description: Description of the primary contaminant types found during inspection (e.g., food waste, non-recyclable plastics, hazardous materials, textiles). Supports contamination tracking and source identification.
Detailed description of corrective actions to be taken. May include rebaling, resorting, process adjustments, or equipment maintenance. Populated when corrective_action_required is true.
Indicates whether corrective action is required based on inspection findings. True when bale must be reworked, reprocessed, or when process improvements are needed.
System timestamp when the inspection record was first created in the database. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

Quality grade assigned to the bale based on inspection results. Determines commodity pricing tier and buyer eligibility. Premium is highest quality, Grade A-C are standard tiers, off-spec requires rework, reject is unsaleable.
Time spent performing the inspection in minutes. Used for labor cost tracking and process efficiency analysis.

Physical location where the inspection was performed. Production line for in-process QC, staging area for pre-shipment, loading dock for final verification, buyer facility for receiving inspection, third party lab for independent verification.
Free-form notes captured by the inspector. May include observations about material quality, equipment issues, or process anomalies.
Business-readable unique identifier for the inspection event. Format: INS-YYYYMMDD-NNNN where YYYYMMDD is inspection date and NNNN is sequence number.

Overall pass/fail result of the inspection. Pass indicates bale meets quality standards, fail requires corrective action, conditional pass allows shipment with buyer notification, pending retest requires additional verification.
Date and time when the bale inspection was performed. Principal business event timestamp for this quality control transaction.

Category of inspection performed. Production QC (Quality Control) occurs during bale production, pre-shipment before delivery, buyer-requested per customer requirement, random audit for ongoing quality assurance, compliance verification for regulatory requirements, or post-complaint following buyer dispute.
System timestamp when the inspection record was last updated. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.

Type of recovered material in the inspected bale. Aligns with commodity categories tracked for recycling diversion rates and commodity sales. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mixed_paper|cardboard|pet_plastic|hdpe_plastic|aluminum|steel|glass|mixed_plastics — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Measured moisture content in the bale as a percentage of total weight. Affects commodity value and grade classification. Expressed as percentage (0.00 to 100.00).
Indicates whether photographic evidence was captured during inspection. True when photos are available for quality documentation or dispute resolution.
Indicates whether the bale must be reinspected after corrective action. True when initial inspection failed or when buyer requires verification.
Detailed explanation of why the bale failed inspection. Populated only when inspection_result is fail. Supports root cause analysis and process improvement.
Number of samples taken from the bale for inspection. Larger sample sizes provide more accurate contamination and moisture measurements.
Explanation of why shipment was not approved. Populated when approved_for_shipment is false. Used for logistics coordination and customer communication.

System of record where the inspection data originated. AMCS for integrated MRF operations, SAP QM (Quality Management) for enterprise quality module, manual entry for paper-based inspections, mobile app for field inspections, third party lab for external certifications.
Unique identifier for this buyer-TSDF return agreement record. Primary key.

description: Foreign key linking to the commodity buyer who has established this contamination return agreement

business_glossary_term: Buyer Tsdf Return Agreement - Tsdf Facility Id
description: Foreign key linking to the TSDF facility authorized to receive contaminated returns under this agreement

Current operational status of this buyer-TSDF return agreement. ACTIVE agreements are in force, SUSPENDED agreements are temporarily inactive, EXPIRED agreements have passed their expiration date, TERMINATED agreements have been formally ended.
Maximum allowable contamination percentage in recovered material bales before rejection and TSDF disposition is triggered under this agreement. Varies by buyer quality standards and commodity type.
Timestamp when this buyer-TSDF return agreement record was first created in the system.

Defines which party bears the financial responsibility for TSDF disposal costs for contaminated returns. Values: BUYER (buyer pays all costs), WM (Waste Management absorbs costs), SHARED (split per agreement terms), NEGOTIATED (case-by-case determination).
Date when this buyer-TSDF return agreement became effective and operational. Used for determining which agreement terms apply to contamination events.
Date when this buyer-TSDF return agreement expires or requires renewal. Null indicates an evergreen agreement with no fixed expiration.
Timestamp when this buyer-TSDF return agreement record was last updated.
Maximum tonnage of contaminated material that can be sent to this TSDF facility under this agreement within a calendar year. Used for capacity planning and agreement compliance monitoring.
Free-text field for capturing additional terms, special conditions, or operational notes specific to this buyer-TSDF return agreement.

Describes the required communication and notification procedures when contaminated material is identified and routed to the TSDF under this agreement. May include contact sequences, documentation requirements, and timeline expectations.

Comma-separated list of EPA hazardous waste codes that this buyer-TSDF agreement is specifically designed to handle. Subset of the TSDF facility's permitted waste codes, tailored to the buyer's typical contamination profile.
Indicates whether the commodity buyer must provide explicit written authorization before contaminated material can be sent to this TSDF facility. Affects operational workflow and liability.
Unique system-generated surrogate identifier for each recovered commodity master record in the Materials Recovery Facility (MRF). Primary key for the commodity reference table. Role: MASTER_RESOURCE.

Narrative description of materials explicitly accepted within this commodity stream (e.g., 'Corrugated containers, kraft paper bags' for OCC). Complements the prohibited materials list to fully define the commodity specification for MRF operations and customer education.

description: Commodity identifier as configured in the AMCS Platform for route management and MRF dispatching. Used to link commodity master records to AMCS recycling route assignments, container tracking, and inbound material receiving workflows.
reference: AMCS Platform Route Optimization and MRF Operations Module

description: Indicates whether this commodity must be baled prior to outbound shipment to end-market buyers. Drives MRF baler scheduling, bale production tracking, and outbound logistics planning. False for loose commodities such as glass cullet or scrap metal.

description: Current or standard base price per ton (USD) for this commodity as used in MRF commodity sales. For positive-value commodities, this is the revenue received per ton sold. For negative-value commodities, this is the cost paid per ton disposed. Sensitive commercial pricing data. Integrated with Oracle Revenue Management and SAP FI/CO.
reference: Oracle Revenue Management; SAP S/4HANA FI/CO; IFRS/GAAP Financial Reporting Standards; SOX Compliance

description: High-level material category grouping for the commodity. Drives MRF sorting line configuration, equipment routing, and EPA diversion rate reporting by material stream. reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Master; ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; AMCS Platform

description: Full descriptive name of the recovered commodity (e.g., 'Old Corrugated Containers', 'High-Density Polyethylene Natural', 'Aluminum Used Beverage Cans'). Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL for this MASTER_RESOURCE and is used in customer-facing reports, commodity sales invoices, and EPA recycling disclosures.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines

description: Current lifecycle status of the commodity master record. Active commodities are processed and sold from MRF operations. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS for this MASTER_RESOURCE.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Master; AMCS Platform Commodity Catalog

description: Fee charged per ton (USD) when a commodity load exceeds the maximum contamination percentage threshold. Applied as a deduction from the commodity sale price or as a separate charge to the originating customer account. Configured in Oracle Revenue Management billing rules.
reference: Oracle Revenue Management; SAP S/4HANA SD; NWRA Contamination Fee Standards

description: Timestamp when this commodity master record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage, audit trail requirements, and SOX-compliant record management. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); IFRS/GAAP Financial Reporting Standards; SAP S/4HANA MM

description: Indicates whether tonnage of this commodity counts toward the diversion rate calculation (percentage of waste diverted from landfill). True for recyclable and compostable commodities; false for residue streams that are landfilled. Drives EPA and state-level diversion rate reporting.

description: Date from which this commodity master record and its associated grade specifications became effective for MRF operations and commodity sales. Used to manage commodity specification version history and ensure correct specifications are applied to historical transactions.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Master; IFRS/GAAP Financial Reporting Standards

description: Indicates whether this commodity is sold to domestic end-market buyers, exported to international markets, or both. description: EPA-assigned material category code used in mandatory recycling and diversion rate reporting submissions. Aligns commodity records with EPA's Advancing Sustainable Materials Management (SMM) reporting framework and state environmental quality department reporting requirements.

description: Date on which this commodity master record or its grade specifications expire and must be reviewed or replaced. Null for open-ended commodity definitions. Supports commodity specification lifecycle management and ensures outdated specifications are not applied to active operations.

description: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emission factor in metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e) per ton of commodity recycled versus landfilled. reference: EPA GHG Reporting Program (40 CFR Part 98); EPA WARM Model; ISO 14001; GHG Protocol

description: Narrative description of the ISRI grade specification including allowable materials, prohibited items, and quality characteristics. Used by MRF quality control staff to assess bale acceptance and by sales teams to communicate product quality to end-market buyers.

description: Standardized grade code assigned by the Institute of Scrap Recycling Industries (ISRI) Scrap Specifications Circular. reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; National Waste and Recycling Association (NWRA) Standards

description: Timestamp when this commodity master record was most recently modified. Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver Layer pipeline, audit trail compliance, and detecting stale commodity specifications. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act); IFRS/GAAP Financial Reporting Standards; SAP S/4HANA MM

description: Indicates whether the commodity generates revenue (positive_value — MRF receives payment from buyer), incurs a cost (negative_value — MRF pays buyer to accept), or is non-marketable residue. Critical for commodity sales pricing strategy, P&L reporting, and Oracle Revenue Management billing configuration.
reference: Oracle Revenue Management; SAP S/4HANA FI/CO; NWRA Market Reporting Standards

business_glossary_term: Maximum Bale Density (lbs per cubic foot)

description: Maximum allowable contamination percentage (by weight) for an accepted bale or load of this commodity. reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines; NWRA Quality Standards

description: Maximum allowable moisture content percentage (by weight) for this commodity. Excess moisture reduces commodity value, increases transportation weight, and may cause rejection by end-market buyers. Used in MRF quality control inspections and bale certification.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; NWRA Quality Standards

description: Maximum number of days this commodity may be stored at the MRF before quality degradation or regulatory limits require outbound shipment. Drives inventory turnover alerts in SAP MM and AMCS commodity inventory management. Critical for hazardous commodities with RCRA storage time limits.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262 Hazardous Waste Generator Standards; SAP S/4HANA MM; OSHA

business_glossary_term: Minimum Bale Density (lbs per cubic foot)
description: Minimum required bale density in pounds per cubic foot for this commodity. Bales below this density threshold may be rejected by buyers or subject to price discounts. Used to configure MRF baling equipment settings and quality control acceptance criteria.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; NWRA Baling Standards

description: Minimum expected processing throughput in tons per day (TPD) for this commodity on the MRF sort line. Used for MRF capacity planning, equipment performance benchmarking, and operational KPI reporting. Below-threshold throughput triggers operational review.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; AMCS Platform MRF Throughput Reporting

description: Description of required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for MRF workers handling this commodity (e.g., 'Cut-resistant gloves, safety glasses' for metals; 'Respirator, chemical-resistant gloves' for hazardous commodities). Supports OSHA compliance and worker safety training programs.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.132 PPE Standards; ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety; Enviance EHS

description: Minimum acceptable sale price per ton (USD) below which the commodity should not be sold without management approval. Used in Oracle Revenue Management to trigger pricing exception workflows and protect MRF revenue margins during market downturns.
reference: Oracle Revenue Management; SAP S/4HANA FI/CO; SOX Compliance; IFRS/GAAP

description: Method by which the commodity sale price is determined: spot (current market spot price), index (tied to a published commodity index such as RISI or AMM), contract (fixed price per sales contract), or negotiated (case-by-case negotiation). Drives Oracle Revenue Management pricing configuration and commodity sales contract terms.
reference: Oracle Revenue Management; SAP SD Pricing; RISI Commodity Index; AMM Metal Prices

description: Narrative description of materials explicitly prohibited from inclusion in this commodity stream (e.g., 'No food-soiled paper, no wax-coated board' for OCC; 'No PVC, no colored HDPE' for natural HDPE). Used by MRF sorting staff, quality control inspectors, and driver education programs to prevent contamination.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) Waste Code
description: EPA-assigned RCRA waste code for hazardous commodities (e.g., D001 for ignitability, F001 for spent solvents). Required on hazardous waste manifests and TSDF disposal documentation. Null for non-hazardous commodities. Tracked in Enviance EHS and SAP EHS module.
reference: RCRA (Resource Conservation and Recovery Act) 40 CFR Part 261; EPA Hazardous Waste Codes

description: Classification of the commodity's recyclability and market demand: tier_1 (high-value, readily recyclable with established markets), tier_2 (moderate-value, recyclable with limited markets), tier_3 (low-value, difficult to recycle), residue (non-recyclable, destined for disposal). Drives diversion rate calculations and sustainability reporting.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems; SWANA

description: Name of the published commodity price index used as the pricing reference for index-priced commodities (e.g., 'RISI OCC Index', 'AMM Aluminum Index', 'Fastmarkets HDPE Index'). Null for spot or contract-priced commodities. Used in Oracle Revenue Management for automated price updates.
reference: Oracle Revenue Management; RISI Commodity Index; AMM Metal Prices; Fastmarkets

description: Society of the Plastics Industry (SPI) Resin Identification Code (RIC) for plastic commodities (1=PET, 2=HDPE, 3=PVC, 4=LDPE, 5=PP, 6=PS, 7=Other). Null for non-plastic commodities. Required for plastics market reporting and end-market buyer specifications. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: 1|2|3|4|5|6|7 — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: ASTM D7611 Plastics Resin Identification Coding System; EPA Recycling Reporting

description: Code identifying the MRF sorting line or processing stream assigned to this commodity (e.g., 'FIBER-1', 'PLASTIC-2', 'METAL-OCC'). Used by AMCS Platform for route-to-sort-line assignment and MRF equipment configuration. Supports throughput (TPD) reporting by sort line.
reference: AMCS Platform MRF Operations Module; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Target or standard weight in pounds for a single bale of this commodity as produced by MRF baling equipment. Used for bale production planning, outbound load configuration, and weight-based pricing reconciliation with end-market buyers.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; NWRA Baling Standards; SAP MM Material Master

description: Storage condition requirement for this commodity at the MRF prior to outbound shipment (e.g., indoor for paper to prevent moisture, hazmat_storage for hazardous commodities, outdoor for metals). Drives MRF facility layout planning and OSHA/EPA storage compliance.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910 Storage Standards; EPA RCRA Storage Requirements; ISO 45001

description: Secondary classification within the material category providing finer segmentation (e.g., 'corrugated' within paper, 'PET bottles' within plastics, 'ferrous' within metals). Used for detailed MRF throughput reporting and commodity-specific market pricing.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) Testing Required Flag
description: Indicates whether Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) testing is required for this commodity prior to disposal or sale. Applicable to commodities that may exhibit hazardous characteristics under RCRA. Triggers laboratory testing workflow in Enviance EHS.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 261.24 TCLP; EPA Hazardous Waste Testing Methods; Enviance EHS

description: Standard unit of measure used for weighing, pricing, and reporting this commodity (e.g., ton for paper/metals, lb for small-volume materials, bale for pre-baled commodities). Aligns with SAP MM base unit of measure and Oracle Revenue Management pricing unit. Serves as the MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE classification for this MASTER_RESOURCE.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Master; NIST Weights and Measures; Oracle Revenue Management

description: Unique system-generated surrogate identifier for each commodity-offering acceptance specification
Foreign key linking to the recovered commodity master
Foreign key linking to the service offering master

Current status of this commodity acceptance under this service offering. Active = currently accepted, Suspended = temporarily not accepted (e.g., due to market conditions or contamination issues), Discontinued = permanently removed from offering.

Comma-separated or JSON list of ISRI grade codes accepted for this commodity under this specific service offering. Allows service offerings to restrict which grades are acceptable (e.g., residential service may only accept Grade A OCC, while commercial accepts Grades A and B).

Maximum allowable contamination percentage for this commodity under this service offering. May differ from the commodity master default to reflect service-level quality requirements (e.g., premium recycling programs have stricter thresholds than standard programs).
Timestamp when this commodity acceptance specification record was created in the system.
Date when this commodity acceptance specification became or will become active for this service offering. Supports versioning of acceptance criteria over time.
Date when this commodity acceptance specification expires or was superseded. Null for currently active specifications. Supports historical tracking of acceptance criteria changes.
User ID or system identifier that last modified this commodity acceptance specification record.
Timestamp when this commodity acceptance specification record was last updated.

Minimum volume in pounds of this commodity required per pickup or billing period for this service offering. Null if no minimum applies. Used for commercial/industrial programs with volume commitments.

Method by which the commodity sale price or revenue share is determined for this commodity-offering combination. Values: spot (current market spot price), indexed (tied to published index), fixed (contracted fixed price), revenue_share (percentage of commodity revenue credited to customer), cost_plus (cost recovery plus margin).
Code indicating why this commodity is not accepted or was suspended under this service offering (e.g., MARKET_COLLAPSE, CONTAMINATION_ISSUE, EQUIPMENT_LIMITATION). Null for active acceptances.
Percentage of commodity sale revenue credited back to the customer under this service offering. Applicable when pricing_basis is revenue_share. Null for other pricing methods.
User ID or system identifier that created this commodity acceptance specification record.
Unique identifier for the commodity buyer record. Primary key for the commodity buyer entity within the recycling domain.
Indicates whether the buyer is currently active and eligible for commodity sales. True means active and available for transactions, False means inactive and excluded from sales processes.
First line of the buyer's billing address including street number and street name. Used for invoicing and accounts receivable processing.
Second line of the buyer's billing address for suite, floor, or building information. Optional field for additional address details.
City name for the buyer's billing address.
Three-letter ISO country code for the buyer's billing address.
Postal or ZIP code for the buyer's billing address.
State or province code for the buyer's billing address. Uses standard postal abbreviations.
Date when the business relationship with this commodity buyer was first established. Used for buyer tenure analysis and relationship management.
Legal or trade name of the commodity buyer organization that purchases recovered materials from MRF operations.

Classification of the commodity buyer based on their role in the recovered materials supply chain. Domestic mills process materials domestically, export brokers facilitate international sales, reprocessors transform materials into new feedstock, direct end-users consume materials in manufacturing, aggregators consolidate materials from multiple sources, and traders buy and resell commodities.
Primary email address for the buyer contact. Used for purchase orders, invoices, shipping notifications, and quality documentation.
Primary telephone number for the buyer contact. Used for order coordination, quality issues, and logistics communication.
Timestamp when this commodity buyer record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail purposes.
Maximum outstanding accounts receivable balance allowed for this buyer in USD. Used for credit risk management and sales order approval workflows.

Current credit approval status of the buyer. Approved buyers can receive shipments on credit terms, suspended buyers require prepayment or letter of credit, declined buyers are not eligible for sales.
Date of the most recent commodity sale transaction with this buyer. Used to identify dormant buyer relationships and trigger reactivation campaigns.
Minimum shipment size in tons that the buyer will accept per order. Used for load planning and sales order validation.
Timestamp when this commodity buyer record was last updated. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.
Free-text field for additional buyer-specific information such as special handling requirements, preferred contact times, facility access instructions, or historical relationship context.
Standard payment terms code defining the number of days and conditions for payment (e.g., Net 30, Net 45, COD, Letter of Credit). Aligns with SAP FI payment terms master data.

Comma-separated list of recovered material commodity types the buyer prefers to purchase (e.g., OCC, mixed paper, PET, HDPE, aluminum, ferrous metals, glass). Supports sales planning and material allocation decisions.

Buyer's preferred logistics arrangement. FOB MRF (Free On Board at Materials Recovery Facility) means buyer arranges transport, delivered means seller delivers to buyer facility, buyer pickup means buyer collects from MRF, third-party carrier means mutually agreed logistics provider.
Full name of the primary business contact person at the buyer organization responsible for commodity procurement and contract management.

Indicates whether the buyer requires quality certification documentation (e.g., contamination reports, bale composition analysis) with each shipment. True means certification is mandatory, False means standard documentation suffices.
reference: ISRI Quality Standards / Buyer Contract Terms

description: SAP SD customer master record number linking this commodity buyer to the enterprise sales and accounts receivable system. Primary reference for commodity sales orders and revenue recognition.

SAP MM vendor master record number linking this commodity buyer to the enterprise procurement and accounts payable system. Used for purchase order and invoice reconciliation when buyer also supplies services or materials.
First line of the buyer's shipping or delivery address. Used for logistics planning and Bill of Lading (BOL) documentation.
Second line of the buyer's shipping address for dock, gate, or facility-specific routing information.
City name for the buyer's shipping or receiving facility.
Three-letter ISO country code for the buyer's shipping destination. Critical for export compliance and international logistics.
Postal or ZIP code for the buyer's shipping facility.
State or province code for the buyer's shipping address.
Buyer organization's tax identification number (EIN in USA, VAT number in EU, or equivalent). Required for tax reporting and compliance with revenue recognition standards.

Unique surrogate identifier for each commodity grade specification record in the Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) quality reference table.
