reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Reference to the commodity_grade_id of the newer grade specification that replaces this record when a grade is deprecated or revised. Null if this is the current active version. Supports grade version lineage tracking and ensures operational systems transition to updated specifications.
reference: SAP MM Material Master Versioning; ISO 14001 Document Control

description: Geographic region or operational division for which this grade specification applies (e.g., 'Northeast', 'Southeast', 'National'). Some grade specifications may vary by region due to local buyer requirements or state recycling regulations. Null or 'National' indicates the grade applies enterprise-wide.
reference: State Environmental Quality Department Recycling Regulations; SWANA Regional Operations

description: Date on which this commodity grade specification was formally approved by the authorized quality manager or operations director. Required for quality management system documentation and regulatory audit readiness.
reference: ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems; SWANA MRF Quality Management; SOX Compliance

description: Name or employee identifier of the MRF quality manager or operations director who approved this grade specification for operational use. Required for quality management system compliance and audit trail. Sourced from Workday HCM employee records.
reference: ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems; ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety; SWANA MRF Quality Management

description: Required or target bale dimensions (length x width x height in inches) for this commodity grade as specified by buyers or ISRI standards (e.g., '60x30x48'). Ensures compatibility with buyer receiving equipment and maximizes trailer load efficiency. Used in baler setup configuration.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; SWANA Baling Operations Standards

description: Indicates whether material classified under this grade requires explicit buyer acceptance confirmation before outbound shipment. True for specialty or off-grade materials where buyers must pre-approve loads. False for standard grades with standing purchase agreements. Drives outbound logistics workflow in AMCS.
reference: SWANA MRF Outbound Operations; Commodity Sales Contract Management

business_glossary_term: Carbon Dioxide Equivalent (CO2e) Avoided per Ton
description: Estimated metric tons of CO2e greenhouse gas emissions avoided per ton of commodity recovered and sold at this grade, compared to virgin material production. Used for GHG emissions reporting, sustainability disclosures, and circular economy impact quantification. Sourced from EPA WARM (Waste Reduction Model) emission factors.
reference: EPA WARM Model; GHG Protocol Scope 3 Reporting; ISO 14064 GHG Quantification; Clean Air Act

description: Color or color mix specification required for this commodity grade (e.g., 'clear only', 'clear and green', 'mixed colors acceptable', 'brown only'). Primarily applicable to glass and PET plastic grades where color separation directly impacts end-market value and processing requirements at buyer facilities.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; Glass Packaging Institute Standards

description: Specific material subtype within the commodity category (e.g., OCC — Old Corrugated Containers, ONP — Old Newsprint, HDPE, PET, Aluminum UBC, Tin/Steel, Clear Glass, Brown Glass). Aligns with ISRI grade designations and SAP MM material classification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: OCC|ONP|SOP|HDPE|PET|PP|aluminum_ubc|tin_steel|clear_glass|brown_glass|green_glass|e-waste — promote to reference product]
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; SAP MM Material Classification

description: Broad material category of the commodity to which this grade applies. Drives sorting line configuration, downstream market routing, and EPA recycling diversion rate reporting. Values: paper, plastic, metal, glass, organics, electronics, mixed. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: paper|plastic|metal|glass|organics|electronics|mixed — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: EPA Advancing Sustainable Materials Management; ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; ISO 14001

description: Timestamp when this commodity grade specification record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and compliance documentation requirements. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per enterprise data standards.
reference: SOX Sarbanes-Oxley Act Audit Trail Requirements; ISO 14001 Document Control; GAAP Record Keeping

description: Indicates whether material sold under this commodity grade qualifies for diversion rate credit in EPA and state recycling program reporting. True for grades that represent genuine material recovery; False for off-grade or contaminated material routed to landfill or WTE. Impacts sustainability KPI reporting and circular economy goal tracking.
reference: EPA Recycling Diversion Rate Reporting; State Environmental Quality Department Recycling Regulations; ISO 14001

description: Indicates whether this commodity grade is eligible for domestic sale only, export sale only, or both. Export eligibility is subject to Basel Convention restrictions on hazardous waste exports and country-specific import regulations. Drives market routing decisions in commodity sales management.
reference: Basel Convention on Hazardous Waste; EPA Export Regulations; DOT International Shipping Requirements

description: Date from which this commodity grade specification becomes effective and applicable for quality control acceptance/rejection decisions and commodity pricing. Enables versioned grade specifications to align with market condition changes or updated ISRI standards.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular (versioning); SAP MM Validity Periods

description: Type of end-market or buyer facility that typically purchases this commodity grade (e.g., 'paper mill', 'plastic reprocessor', 'aluminum smelter', 'glass beneficiator', 'steel mill', 'export broker'). Informs market development strategy and outbound logistics planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: paper_mill|plastic_reprocessor|aluminum_smelter|glass_beneficiator|steel_mill|export_broker|compost_facility|wte_facility — promote to reference product]
reference: SWANA Commodity Markets Report; EPA Recycling Markets Development

description: EPA-assigned commodity classification code used for federal recycling diversion rate reporting and Solid Waste Information System (SWIS) submissions. Enables accurate tracking of material recovery volumes by commodity type for regulatory compliance and sustainability reporting.
reference: EPA Advancing Sustainable Materials Management; EPA SWIS Reporting Requirements; Clean Air Act

description: Date after which this commodity grade specification is no longer valid and must be superseded by a new version. Null indicates the grade specification is open-ended with no planned expiration. Supports versioned grade management when ISRI standards or buyer contract requirements change.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular (versioning); SAP MM Validity Periods

description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the commodity grade specification (e.g., OCC-A, PET-1, ALU-P). Used as the externally-known business identifier in SAP MM material master, AMCS commodity tracking, and buyer purchase orders. Aligns with ISRI commodity grade coding conventions.
reference: Institute of Scrap Recycling Industries (ISRI) Scrap Specifications Circular; SAP MM Material Master

description: Human-readable name of the commodity grade specification (e.g., 'Grade A Old Corrugated Containers', 'Premium Clear PET', 'Standard Mixed Paper', 'Off-Grade Aluminum'). Used in quality control reports, buyer contracts, and MRF operational dashboards.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; SWANA MRF Best Practices

description: Current lifecycle status of the commodity grade specification. Active grades are in use for quality control and pricing. Inactive grades are suspended from use. Deprecated grades have been superseded by updated specifications. Under Review grades are pending revision approval. Controls whether the grade is available for selection in MRF quality control workflows.
reference: SAP MM Material Master Status Management; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Quality tier classification of the grade specification indicating relative market value and purity level. Premium and Grade A command market premiums; Standard meets baseline buyer requirements; Off-Grade triggers price discounts; Rejected material is non-saleable and requires alternative disposition. Drives pricing factor application in Oracle Revenue Management.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Indicates whether this commodity grade involves or may contain hazardous materials subject to RCRA, DOT, or EPA hazardous waste regulations. True triggers mandatory hazardous waste handling protocols, manifest documentation requirements, and TSDF routing. Integrates with Enviance EHS compliance tracking.
reference: RCRA Subtitle C Hazardous Waste Regulations; DOT 49 CFR Hazardous Materials; EPA CERCLA

business_glossary_term: Institute of Scrap Recycling Industries (ISRI) Specification Reference
description: Official ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular grade designation code that this internal grade maps to (e.g., 'ISRI-11' for OCC, 'ISRI-600' for Aluminum Cans). Enables standardized communication with commodity buyers, brokers, and end-markets. Required for export commodity sales documentation.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular (current edition); EPA Recycling Markets

description: Timestamp when this commodity grade specification record was most recently modified. Used to detect stale specifications, trigger review workflows, and maintain data lineage in the Databricks Silver Layer. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per enterprise data standards.
reference: SOX Sarbanes-Oxley Act Audit Trail Requirements; ISO 14001 Document Control

description: Multiplicative premium or discount factor applied to the base commodity market price for this grade (e.g., 1.15 = 15% premium for Premium grade; 0.85 = 15% discount for Off-Grade; 1.00 = no adjustment for Standard). Used in Oracle Revenue Management to calculate commodity sale prices and MRF revenue projections.
reference: Oracle Revenue Management Pricing Rules; SWANA Commodity Market Pricing Guidelines

description: Maximum allowable bale weight in pounds for this commodity grade. Ensures compliance with DOT weight regulations for transport and safe handling limits for forklift and loading equipment. Bales exceeding this limit require splitting before outbound shipment.
reference: DOT 49 CFR Part 393 Vehicle Weight Regulations; OSHA Material Handling Standards

description: Maximum percentage of non-target or prohibited materials allowable in a bale or load for this grade to be accepted by buyers (e.g., 2.00 for Grade A OCC = max 2% contamination). Exceeding this threshold triggers grade downgrade or rejection. Used in MRF quality control acceptance/rejection decisions and contamination tracking.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; SWANA MRF Contamination Standards; EPA Recycling Program Guidelines

description: Maximum allowable moisture content percentage for this commodity grade. Excess moisture reduces commodity value, increases transport weight, and can cause material degradation. Measured at bale production or outbound load inspection. Critical for paper and fiber grades where moisture directly impacts pulp mill acceptance.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; TAPPI Moisture Testing Standards; SWANA MRF Best Practices

description: Maximum allowable individual particle or item size in inches for material classified under this grade. Oversized items can damage processing equipment at end-market facilities and may trigger load rejection. Particularly relevant for glass, metal, and plastic grades.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; SWANA MRF Equipment Specifications

business_glossary_term: Minimum Bale Density (lbs per cubic ft)
description: Minimum required bale density in pounds per cubic foot for this commodity grade. Ensures structural integrity during transport and storage, and maximizes trailer payload efficiency. Bales failing density requirements may be rejected by buyers or require re-baling. Monitored via baler equipment sensors integrated with AMCS.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; SWANA Baling Operations Standards

description: Minimum required percentage of the target commodity material in a bale or load for this grade classification (e.g., 98.00 for Premium Aluminum = minimum 98% pure aluminum content). Complements the contamination threshold by specifying the positive purity floor rather than the negative contamination ceiling.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; SWANA MRF Quality Standards

description: Minimum weight in pounds of material sample required for quality control testing under this grade specification. Ensures statistical validity of contamination and purity measurements. Applies when sort_purity_test_method is grab_sample or full_sort.
reference: ASTM D5231 Standard Test Method; SWANA MRF Quality Control Procedures

description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, buyer-specific requirements, special handling instructions, or clarifications related to this commodity grade specification. May include references to specific buyer contracts, seasonal market conditions, or equipment-specific processing notes.

Comma-delimited list of materials explicitly prohibited from inclusion in this commodity grade (e.g., 'food waste, hazardous materials, medical waste, batteries, Styrofoam, plastic bags'). Any presence of prohibited materials may result in load rejection, buyer chargebacks, or regulatory violations. Referenced during MRF sorting quality audits and inbound load inspections.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; RCRA Hazardous Waste Regulations; EPA Recycling Contamination Guidelines

description: Default disposition action for material that fails to meet this grade specification. Landfill routes rejected material to disposal; Reprocess returns material to the MRF sorting line; Downgrade reclassifies to a lower grade; Return to Sender sends contaminated loads back to the collection route origin; WTE (Waste-to-Energy) routes to energy recovery. Drives operational workflow in AMCS.
reference: EPA Solid Waste Disposal Regulations; SWANA MRF Operations; RCRA Subtitle D

description: Indicates whether material classified under this grade requires laboratory analysis (e.g., TCLP — Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure testing, moisture analysis, or purity assay) before sale or shipment. True for grades with strict purity or regulatory requirements. Triggers lab sample workflow in Enviance EHS.
reference: EPA TCLP Testing Requirements (40 CFR Part 261); RCRA; Enviance EHS

description: Quality control testing method used to verify that a bale or load meets this grade specification. Visual Sort is a manual inspector review; Grab Sample is a representative sample extraction; Full Sort is complete material separation and weighing; Lab Analysis is laboratory chemical or physical testing; Automated Sensor uses optical or NIR sorting equipment data.
reference: SWANA MRF Quality Control Procedures; ASTM D5231 Standard Test Method for Composition of Unprocessed MSW

description: Sequential version number of this commodity grade specification record. Incremented each time the grade specification is revised (e.g., contamination threshold updated, ISRI reference changed). Enables audit trail of specification changes and ensures quality control decisions reference the correct version.
reference: SAP MM Change Management; SWANA MRF Quality Management Systems; ISO 14001 Document Control

Required frequency of compliance testing or sampling for this commodity under this regulation (e.g., TCLP testing frequency for hazardous commodities, contamination testing for recyclables). Frequency varies by commodity-regulation combination.
User ID or system identifier of the person or process that created this applicability mapping record.

description: Indicates whether this recycling report was submitted after the regulatory submission deadline. True when submission_date exceeds submission_deadline_date. Supports compliance risk monitoring and regulatory penalty tracking.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; RCRA Compliance Deadlines; State Solid Waste Reporting Requirements

description: Total weight in short tons of ferrous and non-ferrous metal commodities (aluminum, steel, tin) recovered and diverted from landfill during the reporting period. Required for material-specific recovery reporting to EPA and state agencies.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Material-Specific Reporting; ISRI Scrap Specifications; RCRA Subtitle D

description: Total weight in short tons of organic materials (food waste, yard waste, compostables) recovered and diverted from landfill during the reporting period. Increasingly required by state organics diversion mandates.
reference: EPA Sustainable Materials Management; State Organics Diversion Requirements; RCRA Subtitle D

description: Total weight in short tons of recovered materials not classified under paper, plastic, metal, glass, or organics categories (e.g., electronics, textiles, rubber) during the reporting period.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Material-Specific Reporting; RCRA Subtitle D

description: Total weight in short tons of paper and cardboard commodities (OCC, ONP, mixed paper) recovered and diverted from landfill during the reporting period. Required for material-specific recovery reporting to EPA and state agencies.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Material-Specific Reporting; ISRI Scrap Specifications; RCRA Subtitle D

description: Total weight in short tons of plastic commodities (PET, HDPE, mixed plastics) recovered and diverted from landfill during the reporting period. Required for material-specific recovery reporting to EPA and state agencies.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Material-Specific Reporting; ASTM D7611 Plastic Identification; RCRA Subtitle D

description: Number of operational days the MRF processed inbound recyclable material during the reporting period. Used to calculate average daily throughput (Tons Per Day) for regulatory performance benchmarking.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; SWANA MRF Performance Standards

description: The regulatory body to which this recycling report is submitted. EPA indicates federal Environmental Protection Agency; state_environmental_agency indicates the applicable state environmental quality department; local_solid_waste_authority indicates a county or municipal solid waste authority; multi_agency indicates simultaneous submission to multiple regulatory bodies.
reference: U.S. EPA Recycling Program; State Environmental Quality Departments; Local Solid Waste Authorities; RCRA

description: Full legal name of the specific regulatory agency receiving this report (e.g., 'Texas Commission on Environmental Quality', 'California Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery'). Provides the precise agency identity beyond the classification in regulatory_agency.
reference: State Environmental Quality Departments; U.S. EPA; Local Solid Waste Authorities

description: Official tracking or confirmation number assigned by the regulatory agency upon receipt or acceptance of the recycling report. Used for correspondence, audit trails, and compliance verification with the agency.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; RCRA Compliance Tracking; State SWIS

description: Description of the reason(s) provided by the regulatory agency for rejecting the recycling report submission. Populated when report_status is 'rejected'. Used to guide resubmission corrections and track compliance issues.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; State Solid Waste Reporting Requirements; Enviance EHS Compliance Tracking

description: Free-text field for operational notes, explanatory comments, or supplemental context associated with this recycling report submission. May include explanations for anomalous tonnage figures, facility disruptions, or agency correspondence notes.
reference: Enviance EHS Platform; Waste Management Internal Compliance Documentation Standards

description: Externally-known business identifier assigned to this recycling report submission, used for tracking and correspondence with regulatory agencies. Typically formatted as a facility-year-sequence code (e.g., MRF-2024-001).
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; State Solid Waste Reporting Requirements

description: Full name of the Waste Management employee responsible for preparing and compiling this recycling report. Required on regulatory submissions for accountability and agency correspondence.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; SOX Compliance; Enviance EHS Workflow

description: Job title of the Waste Management employee who prepared this recycling report (e.g., 'Environmental Compliance Manager', 'MRF Operations Director'). Required on regulatory submissions.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; Enviance EHS Workflow

description: Current lifecycle status of the recycling report submission. Draft indicates report is being prepared; submitted indicates it has been sent to the regulatory agency; accepted indicates agency confirmation of receipt and compliance; rejected indicates agency returned the report for correction; under_review indicates agency is actively reviewing the submission.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; Enviance EHS Submission Workflow

description: Classification of the recycling report by its regulatory purpose. Annual recycling tonnage reports total materials recovered; diversion rate reports percentage of waste diverted from landfill; material-specific recovery reports recovery by commodity type; quarterly performance reports interim operational metrics; facility summary reports aggregate MRF operational data. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: annual_recycling_tonnage|diversion_rate|material_specific_recovery|quarterly_performance|facility_summary|other — promote to reference product]
reference: EPA RCRA Subtitle C Reporting; State Solid Waste Information System (SWIS); SWANA Reporting Standards

description: Last calendar date of the reporting period covered by this recycling report. Combined with reporting_period_start_date defines the exact temporal scope of all tonnage and performance data in the report.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; RCRA Subtitle D; State Solid Waste Reporting Requirements

description: First calendar date of the reporting period covered by this recycling report. Combined with reporting_period_end_date defines the exact temporal scope of all tonnage and performance data in the report.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; RCRA Subtitle D; State Solid Waste Reporting Requirements

description: Frequency classification of the reporting period covered by this submission. Determines the temporal scope of the recycling performance data included in the report.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; RCRA Subtitle D Reporting Requirements

description: Total weight in short tons of material received at the MRF that could not be recovered and was disposed of as residue (landfilled) during the reporting period. Residue rate is a key MRF efficiency metric reported to regulatory agencies.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; SWANA MRF Performance Standards; RCRA Subtitle D

description: Indicates whether this report is a resubmission of a previously rejected or corrected report. True when this record represents a corrected resubmission; False for original submissions. Supports audit trail and compliance history tracking.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; RCRA Compliance Tracking; Enviance EHS Workflow

description: State-issued solid waste facility permit number associated with the MRF at the time of this report submission. Required on state recycling reports to link the submission to the permitted facility.
reference: State Environmental Quality Departments; State Solid Waste Permit Requirements; RCRA Subtitle D

description: Total weight in short tons of all inbound material received at the MRF during the reporting period, including both recyclable and residue streams. Used as the denominator for diversion rate calculation.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; RCRA Subtitle D; SWANA Recycling Metrics Standards

description: Total weight in short tons of all recovered materials processed and diverted from landfill during the reporting period across all commodity streams at the MRF. This is the primary quantitative outcome metric of the recycling report.
reference: EPA Recycling Program Reporting Guidelines; RCRA Subtitle D; SWANA Recycling Metrics Standards

description: Timestamp when this EPA recycling report record was last modified in the Waste Management lakehouse. Updated on every status change, data correction, or agency response update. Supports audit trail and change tracking.
reference: SOX Compliance; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems; Waste Management Data Governance Standards

description: Unique identifier for this equipment certification record. Primary key for the association.
Employee ID of the instructor or supervisor who certified this employee on this equipment. Used for audit trail and training program management.
Foreign key linking to the employee who holds certification to operate the equipment
Foreign key linking to the MRF processing equipment asset that requires operator certification

Current authorization status for this employee-equipment certification. Identified in detection phase as relationship-specific data. Determines whether employee can be scheduled to operate this equipment.
Date when the employee was certified to operate this specific equipment. Identified in detection phase as relationship-specific data.
Date when this equipment certification expires and requires renewal. Identified in detection phase as relationship-specific data. Critical for compliance monitoring.
Number of safety incidents recorded for this employee operating this specific equipment. Used for safety performance tracking and recertification decisions.
Date of the most recent proficiency assessment for this employee on this equipment. Used to track ongoing competency verification.
Scheduled date for the next proficiency assessment. Used for compliance scheduling and training program management.
Free-text notes regarding restrictions, special conditions, or observations related to this certification (e.g., 'Authorized for day shift only', 'Requires supervision for first 40 hours').

Assessed proficiency level of the employee operating this specific equipment. Identified in detection phase as relationship-specific data. Used for shift assignment and complex operation authorization.
Cumulative hours this employee has operated this specific equipment. Used for experience tracking and proficiency advancement decisions.
Date when the employee completed required training for this equipment. Identified in detection phase as relationship-specific data. Used for OSHA recordkeeping.
Unique system-generated identifier for each facility-initiative participation record

business_glossary_term: Facility Initiative Participation - Carbon Initiative Id
description: Foreign key linking to the carbon reduction initiative being implemented at the facility

business_glossary_term: Facility Initiative Participation - Mrf Facility Id
description: Foreign key linking to the MRF facility participating in the carbon initiative
Actual measured annual CO2e reduction in metric tons achieved at this facility after initiative implementation. Null until post-implementation measurement is completed.
Facility-specific baseline annual emissions in metric tons CO2e measured prior to initiative implementation, used to calculate actual reduction achieved at this facility.

Projected or actual annual CO2e reduction in metric tons attributable to this specific facility's participation in this initiative. Facility-level contribution that rolls up to the initiative's total target_co2e_reduction_tons.
Capital investment allocated to this specific facility for implementing this carbon initiative. Facility-level investment that rolls up to the initiative's total capital_investment_amount.
Name of the facility-level project manager or site lead responsible for implementing this initiative at this specific MRF facility.

Role or phase designation for this facility within the initiative. Values include: pilot (testing/proof-of-concept site), full_implementation (standard rollout), phase_1/phase_2 (staged deployment), control_group (baseline comparison facility).

Current implementation status of this carbon initiative at this specific facility. Values: planned (scheduled but not started), in_progress (actively implementing), completed (fully implemented and operational), on_hold (temporarily paused), cancelled (discontinued at this facility).
Free-text notes capturing facility-specific implementation details, challenges, lessons learned, or deviations from standard initiative approach.
Date when this specific MRF facility completed implementation of this carbon initiative or ceased participation. Null if participation is ongoing.

Date when this specific MRF facility began participating in or implementing this carbon initiative. May differ from the initiative's overall planned_start_date due to phased rollout across facilities.
Unique identifier for this facility-permit assignment record. Primary key.
Foreign key linking to the MRF facility that holds this permit
Foreign key linking to the environmental permit held by the facility
Date on which this permit was formally assigned or associated with this facility in Waste Management's compliance tracking system. Used for audit trail and historical tracking.

Name of the Waste Management compliance officer specifically assigned to manage this permit at this facility. May differ from the general permit compliance officer if facility-level assignments exist.
Current compliance status of this facility with respect to this specific permit. Tracks whether the facility is meeting all conditions, limits, and reporting requirements imposed by this permit.
Date on which this permit became effective and binding for this specific facility. May differ from the permit's original issue date if the permit was transferred or amended for this facility.

Date on which this permit expires for this specific facility. Critical for renewal tracking and compliance planning. May differ from the master permit expiration if facility-specific amendments exist.
Additional conditions, limitations, or requirements specific to this facility's use of this permit. Supplements the general permit conditions with facility-specific operational constraints.
Date on which the most recent compliance report for this permit at this facility was submitted to the regulatory agency. Used to track reporting frequency adherence.
Date of the most recent regulatory inspection conducted for this specific permit at this specific facility. Used to track inspection frequency and schedule future inspections.
Date by which the next compliance report for this permit at this facility must be submitted to the regulatory agency. Critical for avoiding reporting violations.
Anticipated or scheduled date for the next regulatory inspection of this permit at this facility. Used for compliance planning and resource allocation.

The functional role or purpose this permit serves at this specific facility. A facility may hold multiple permits serving different regulatory purposes (e.g., one for air emissions, one for water discharge, one for waste handling).
Date on which this permit was terminated, revoked, or otherwise ceased to be applicable to this facility. Null if the permit is still active.
Unique system-generated identifier for each inbound material load received at the Materials Recovery Facility (MRF). Serves as the primary key for all load-level transactions and reconciliations.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; SAP MM Material Document

description: Reference to the customer account (residential, commercial, or municipal) associated with this inbound load. Used for tipping fee billing reconciliation in Oracle Revenue Management and Salesforce CRM account linkage.
reference: Oracle Revenue Management; Salesforce CRM; SAP SD

description: Foreign key linking to sustainability.diversion_record. Business justification: Each inbound load contributes tonnage to facility-level diversion metrics tracked for ESG reporting and regulatory compliance. Business need: Diversion rate calculation, ESG metric aggregation, tracea
Reference to the CDL-licensed driver who delivered the inbound load. Used for driver performance tracking, DOT compliance, and load accountability.
reference: DOT Commercial Driver License (CDL) Requirements; Workday HCM

description: Reference to the MRF scale house operator who processed this inbound load weigh-in. Used for operator accountability, training compliance tracking, and audit trail requirements.
reference: OSHA Recordkeeping; SOX Compliance; Workday HCM

description: Reference to the Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) that received this inbound load. Supports multi-facility operations and facility-level throughput reporting.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

business_glossary_term: Generator Epa Id Registration Id (Foreign Key)
description: Foreign key linking to hazmat.epa_id_registration. Business justification: MRFs receiving contaminated loads from generators must track EPA ID registrations for regulatory compliance and enforcement. When hazardous contamination exceeds thresholds, generator EPA ID is requir

Foreign key linking to safety.incident. Business justification: Incidents during load tipping (driver injuries, contamination exposure, vehicle accidents) require linkage to the specific inbound load for root cause analysis, customer notification, and contaminatio
FK to recycling.mrf_facility.mrf_facility_id — Every inbound load must reference which MRF received it. Required for facility throughput reporting and contamination rate tracking by facility.

Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_order. Business justification: Buy-back programs and commercial recyclable purchases require linking inbound loads to originating POs for three-way matching (receipt, PO, invoice), cost reconciliation, and purchased material tracea

Reference to the collection route that generated this inbound load. Links the MRF receipt back to the originating residential or commercial collection route for AMCS route-to-MRF load reconciliation and diversion rate reporting.
reference: AMCS Platform Route Management; EPA Recycling Reporting

description: Reference to the transfer station that consolidated and dispatched this load to the MRF, if applicable. Null for direct-haul loads from collection routes. Supports transfer station throughput and chain-of-custody tracking.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; EPA Recycling Reporting

description: Reference to the fleet vehicle that delivered the inbound load to the MRF. Used for fleet performance tracking, load-per-vehicle analytics, and Geotab telematics reconciliation.
reference: AMCS Platform; Geotab Fleet Telematics; DOT Vehicle Records

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.permit. Business justification: Inbound loads must comply with facility waste acceptance permits specifying allowed material types, contamination limits, and capacity thresholds. Critical for scale house permit verification and regu

Reference identifier from the AMCS Platform linking this MRF inbound load record to the originating route dispatch and collection event. Enables route-to-MRF load reconciliation and confirms that collected materials were delivered to the correct facility.
reference: AMCS Platform Route and Load Management; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Bill of Lading number associated with this inbound load, used for third-party hauler loads and transfer station deliveries. Provides chain-of-custody documentation and supports SAP MM goods receipt matching.
reference: DOT Freight Regulations; SAP MM Goods Receipt; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Indicates whether the inbound load was visually identified as contaminated at the time of receipt. True = contamination detected; False = load appears clean. Triggers contamination workflow including surcharge assessment, customer notification, and Enviance EHS incident logging if contamination exceeds threshold.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting; SWANA MRF Operations Standards; ISO 14001

description: Initial visual estimate of contamination level as a percentage of total load volume, assessed by the MRF receiving operator at the tipping floor. Expressed as 0.00 to 100.00. Used for contamination trending, customer education programs, and EPA recycling quality reporting. Formal contamination rate may be updated after sort audit.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting; SWANA MRF Operations Standards; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

description: Additional fee assessed on this load due to contamination exceeding the contractual threshold, expressed in US dollars. Applied per customer contract terms when contamination percentage exceeds the agreed acceptable contamination rate. Posted to Oracle Revenue Management for billing.
reference: Oracle Revenue Management; SAP SD; IFRS/GAAP; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Primary category of contamination identified in the load (e.g., food waste, hazardous materials, non-recyclable plastics, bagged recyclables, electronics, textiles, medical waste). Used for contamination root cause analysis and targeted customer outreach. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: food_waste|hazardous|non_recyclable_plastic|bagged_recyclables|electronics|textiles|medical_waste|other — promote to reference product]
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting; SWANA MRF Operations Standards; RCRA Subtitle D

description: Date and time the inbound load record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: SOX Compliance; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Estimated tonnage of this load that is expected to be diverted from landfill through recycling or recovery, based on material stream type and historical contamination-adjusted yield rates. Expressed in short tons. Used for real-time diversion rate tracking and EPA recycling program reporting. Distinct from actual recovered commodity weight which is captured at bale production.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting; SWANA Diversion Rate Methodology; ISO 14001

description: Total weight of the loaded vehicle as measured at the MRF inbound scale, expressed in short tons. Gross weight is the first weigh-in measurement before tare deduction. Critical for Tons Per Day (TPD) throughput reporting and tipping fee calculation.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; NIST Handbook 44 Weights and Measures; EPA Recycling Reporting

description: Indicates whether this inbound load has been selected for and completed a formal sort audit or waste characterization study. True = audit completed. Sort audits are used to validate contamination estimates, measure commodity composition, and support EPA recycling program reporting accuracy.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting; SWANA Sort Audit Methodology; ISO 14001

description: Free-text field for scale operator or supervisor notes regarding this inbound load. May include observations about load quality, unusual materials, driver communications, or special handling instructions. Supports operational exception management.

Classification of how the load arrived at the MRF. 'direct_haul' = collection vehicle delivering directly from route; 'transfer_station' = consolidated load from a transfer station; 'drop_off_center' = aggregated materials from a public drop-off facility; 'special_event' = community recycling event; 'third_party_hauler' = independent hauler delivering under contract.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; EPA Recycling Reporting; AMCS Platform

description: Current workflow state of the inbound load record. 'received' = weighed and logged at scale; 'accepted' = cleared for processing; 'rejected' = refused entry (contamination, wrong material, etc.); 'pending_review' = flagged for supervisor review; 'posted' = SAP MM material receipt posted; 'voided' = record cancelled.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; SAP MM Goods Receipt Workflow

description: Hazardous waste tracking manifest number, if applicable. Required under RCRA for loads containing any hazardous waste fraction. Null for standard recyclable loads. Links to Enviance EHS manifest tracking for regulatory compliance.
reference: RCRA Subtitle C; EPA Hazardous Waste Manifest System; Enviance EHS

description: Classification of the inbound material stream. 'single_stream_residential' = commingled recyclables from residential curbside collection; 'commercial_mixed' = mixed recyclables from commercial accounts; 'cnd' = Construction and Demolition (C&D) debris; 'drop_off' = materials from public drop-off programs; 'organics' = food/yard waste streams; 'special_collection' = event or special program collections. Drives sorting line configuration and commodity yield expectations.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting; SWANA MRF Operations Standards; RCRA Subtitle D

description: Net weight of the inbound material load, calculated as gross weight minus tare weight, expressed in short tons. This is the primary tonnage figure used for TPD throughput reporting, tipping fee billing, diversion rate calculations, and SAP MM material receipt posting.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting; SWANA MRF Operations Standards; SAP MM Goods Receipt; NIST Handbook 44

description: Work shift during which this inbound load was received and processed at the MRF. Used for shift-level throughput reporting, labor allocation, and operational performance benchmarking.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; Workday HCM Shift Management

description: Date and time the hauling vehicle arrived at the MRF scale house and the load receipt process was initiated. This is the principal business event timestamp for the inbound load transaction. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; EPA Recycling Reporting; AMCS Platform

description: Identifier of the MRF tipping floor dock or bay assigned to receive this load. Used for floor traffic management, sorting line assignment, and operational throughput balancing across dock positions.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; AMCS Platform

description: Reason code or description explaining why a load was rejected at the MRF gate. Populated only when load_status = 'rejected'. Common reasons include excessive contamination, prohibited materials, missing documentation, or capacity constraints. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: excessive_contamination|prohibited_materials|missing_documentation|capacity_exceeded|wrong_material_type|hazardous_detected|other — promote to reference product]
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; EPA Recycling Reporting; RCRA

description: SAP MM material document number generated upon goods receipt posting for this inbound load. Confirms the load has been formally received into SAP inventory management. Null until load_status = 'posted'. Enables reconciliation between MRF scale records and SAP MM inventory.
reference: SAP MM Goods Receipt; SAP S/4HANA MM Module; IFRS/GAAP Inventory Recognition

description: Externally-visible scale house ticket number assigned at the weigh station upon load receipt. Used as the primary operational reference for load reconciliation between the MRF, hauling contractor, and SAP MM material receipt posting. Printed on the physical scale ticket given to the driver.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; SAP MM Goods Receipt; AMCS Load Management

description: Code identifying the geographic service area or municipality from which this load originated. Used for municipal contract compliance reporting, diversion rate calculations by jurisdiction, and EPA recycling program reporting.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting; Local Solid Waste Authorities; SWANA

description: Identifier of the MRF sorting line or processing line to which this load was directed after tipping floor receipt. Used for equipment utilization tracking, throughput balancing, and sort line performance analytics.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; Infor EAM Asset Management

description: Indicates whether this load record has been flagged for or has undergone supervisor review. True = supervisor review required or completed. Triggered by contamination above threshold, weight anomalies, rejected loads, or missing documentation.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; ISO 14001; SOX Internal Controls

description: Date and time the supervisor completed review of this flagged load record. Null if supervisor_review_flag is False or review is pending. Used for SLA compliance on review turnaround and audit trail.
reference: SOX Internal Controls; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

description: Weight of the empty hauling vehicle as measured at the MRF outbound scale after unloading, expressed in short tons. Used with gross weight to calculate net material weight. May be sourced from vehicle tare records if a second weigh is not performed.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; NIST Handbook 44 Weights and Measures

description: Total tipping fee charged for this inbound load in US dollars, calculated as net weight multiplied by the tipping fee rate. Represents the gross revenue amount for this load transaction. Posted to Oracle Revenue Management and SAP FI/CO for billing and GL recognition.
reference: Oracle Revenue Management; SAP FI/CO; IFRS/GAAP Revenue Recognition; SOX Compliance

description: The contractual tipping fee rate applied to this load, expressed in US dollars per short ton. Tipping fees are the charge assessed per ton for waste or recyclable material disposal/processing at the MRF. Rate may vary by material stream type, customer contract, or municipal agreement.
reference: Oracle Revenue Management; SAP SD Pricing; IFRS/GAAP Revenue Recognition

description: Date and time the inbound load record was most recently modified. Tracks post-receipt corrections such as weight adjustments, contamination re-assessments, or status changes.
reference: SOX Compliance; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Type of collection or hauling vehicle that delivered the load. ASL = Automated Side Loader; FEL = Front End Loader; REL = Rear End Loader; roll_off = roll-off container truck; transfer_trailer = semi-trailer from transfer station; rear_load = rear-loading compactor. Affects expected compaction ratio and material quality.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; DOT Vehicle Classification; AMCS Platform

description: Weather condition at the MRF at the time of load receipt. Used for operational analytics correlating weather with contamination rates, load volumes, and processing throughput. Supports capacity planning and seasonal trend analysis.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; EPA Recycling Reporting

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each material composition analysis record at the Materials Recovery Facility (MRF). Primary key for this transactional entity.

Reference to the collection route from which the sampled inbound load originated. Enables contamination trending by geographic route or service area, supporting targeted customer education programs and route-level diversion rate analysis.
reference: AMCS Platform Route Management; EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines

description: Foreign key linking to sustainability.diversion_record. Business justification: Material composition analysis determines what percentage of input stream is diverted vs. landfilled, feeding diversion records. Business need: Diversion rate validation, contamination impact quantific
Reference to the MRF facility where the material composition analysis was performed. Links to the facility master record.
reference: EPA RCRA Facility Reporting; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Reference to the inbound material load (truck delivery or collection route drop-off) that was sampled for this composition analysis. Nullable when analysis is performed on a sort session sample rather than a specific inbound load.
reference: AMCS Platform Inbound Load Tracking; EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines

description: Reference to the Infor EAM asset record for the NIR (Near-Infrared) optical sorter or scanner used when analysis_method is nir_scan. Null for manual sort audit analyses. Supports equipment performance tracking and calibration compliance.
reference: Infor EAM Asset Management; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Reference to the Workday HCM workforce record of the technician or analyst who performed the material composition analysis.
reference: Workday HCM Workforce Records; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Reference to the MRF sort line where the sample was collected or processed. Links to the recycling.sort_line product for sort line configuration and throughput context. Supports sort line performance benchmarking and contamination trending by line.
reference: AMCS Platform Sort Line Tracking; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Reference to the MRF sort line session from which the sample was drawn for composition analysis. Nullable when analysis is tied directly to an inbound load rather than a sort session.
reference: AMCS Platform Sort Session Tracking; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Foreign key linking to hazmat.waste_profile. Business justification: Material composition analyses detecting hazardous constituents (batteries, electronics, chemicals) trigger waste profiling requirements for proper characterization and disposal. Real business process:

Percentage by weight of aluminum (primarily UBC — Used Beverage Cans) in the analyzed sample. Aluminum is the highest-value metal commodity recovered at MRFs. Tracked for commodity recovery, diversion rate, and SAP MM inventory valuation.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines; LME Aluminum Commodity Standards

description: The technique used to perform the material composition analysis. Manual sort audit involves physical hand-sorting of a sample; NIR (Near-Infrared) scan uses optical sensor technology; grab sample is a single-point collection; composite sample aggregates multiple grab samples across a shift or load.
reference: ASTM D5231 Standard Test Method for Determination of the Composition of Unprocessed Municipal Solid Waste; EPA Recycling Measurement Guidance

description: Externally-visible business identifier for this composition analysis record, formatted as MC-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}. Used for cross-referencing with EPA recycling reports, audit documentation, and SAP MM commodity inventory records.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines; SAP MM Material Document Numbering

description: Current lifecycle status of the material composition analysis record. Draft indicates data entry in progress; pending_review awaits QC supervisor sign-off; approved indicates validated and accepted for reporting; rejected indicates failed QC review; voided indicates cancelled or superseded record.
reference: ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems; SWANA MRF Quality Control Standards

description: The principal real-world date and time when the material composition analysis was physically performed at the MRF. Distinct from record creation audit timestamp. Used for contamination trending and EPA recycling reporting period alignment.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Percentage by weight of clear (flint) glass in the analyzed sample. Clear glass commands the highest glass commodity price and is tracked separately from colored glass for accurate market valuation and EPA reporting.
reference: Glass Packaging Institute Standards; EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines

description: Percentage by weight of colored glass (amber, green) in the analyzed sample. Colored glass has lower commodity value than clear glass and is tracked separately for accurate diversion rate and market pricing analysis.
reference: Glass Packaging Institute Standards; EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines

description: Percentage by weight of non-recyclable contaminants (hazardous materials, food-soiled items, non-accepted materials, residue) in the analyzed sample. Critical KPI for MRF operations, commodity quality, and EPA recycling program compliance. High contamination triggers customer outreach and education programs.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines; SWANA MRF Contamination Standards; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Audit timestamp recording when this material composition analysis record was first created in the system. Populated automatically at record insertion. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver layer lakehouse processing.
reference: SOX Compliance Requirements; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Standards

description: The estimated recyclable material percentage from this analysis that contributes to the facility diversion rate calculation (total recyclables recovered / total material received). Equals 100% minus contamination% minus residue%. Used for EPA recycling program reporting and circular economy goal tracking.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines; SWANA Diversion Rate Calculation Standards; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Free-text description of any hazardous or household hazardous waste materials identified in the sample. Populated only when hazardous_material_found is True. Supports RCRA incident reporting, Enviance EHS documentation, and DOT compliance.
reference: RCRA Subtitle C; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200; DOT 49 CFR Hazardous Materials Regulations; Enviance EHS

description: Indicates whether any hazardous or household hazardous waste (HHW) materials were identified in the sample during analysis. True triggers mandatory incident reporting per RCRA and Enviance EHS protocols. Critical for worker safety (OSHA) and regulatory compliance.
reference: RCRA Subtitle C Hazardous Waste Regulations; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 Hazard Communication; Enviance EHS Incident Reporting

description: Percentage by weight of HDPE (High-Density Polyethylene, Resin Code #2) plastics in the analyzed sample. HDPE includes milk jugs and detergent bottles. Tracked separately as a distinct commodity grade with its own market pricing.
reference: ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines; ASTM Resin Identification Codes

description: Classification of the material stream being analyzed. Single stream combines all recyclables; dual stream separates fiber from containers; source separated isolates specific commodities; MSW (Municipal Solid Waste) is mixed waste; C&D (Construction and Demolition) waste is construction debris.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting Guidelines; SWANA MRF Operations Standards; RCRA Subtitle D

description: Percentage by weight of mixed paper (office paper, magazines, junk mail, paperboard) in the analyzed sample. Mixed paper is a lower-grade fiber commodity. Tracked for diversion rate reporting and commodity market pricing.

description: Estimated percentage of the inbound material stream composed of paper and fiber commodities (OCC, ONP, mixed paper) at session start. Used for commodity recovery planning and sort line configuration.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting Requirements; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Estimated percentage of the inbound material stream composed of plastic commodities (PET, HDPE, mixed plastics) at session start. Used for commodity recovery planning and sort line configuration.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting Requirements; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Number of quality control samples taken during this sort session to assess commodity purity and contamination levels. Supports statistical validity of contamination rate measurements and MRF quality assurance programs.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Overall quality grade assigned to the commodity output of this sort session based on contamination levels and commodity purity. Drives commodity pricing and market acceptance. 'off_spec' indicates material outside buyer specifications; 'rejected' indicates material refused by commodity buyer.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; ISRI Scrap Specifications Circular; EPA Recycling Reporting

description: Total weight in short tons of all recovered recyclable commodities (paper, plastics, metals, glass) produced during this sort session. Used for diversion rate calculation and commodity inventory reconciliation in SAP MM.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting Requirements; RCRA Subtitle D; SAP MM — Commodity Inventory

description: Total weight in short tons of non-recoverable residue (contamination and non-recyclable material) sent to landfill disposal after sorting. Used to calculate the diversion rate and residue rate for EPA reporting.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting Requirements; RCRA Subtitle D; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Indicates whether a safety incident (injury, near-miss, or OSHA recordable event) occurred during this sort session. When True, triggers linkage to an incident record in Enviance EHS. Supports OSHA 300 log reporting and safety performance tracking.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1904 — Recordkeeping; Enviance EHS — Incident Management; ISO 45001

description: Calendar date on which the sort session occurred. Used for daily Tons Per Day (TPD) aggregation, EPA recycling reporting, and operational scheduling alignment.
reference: EPA Recycling Reporting Requirements; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Total elapsed time in minutes from session start to session end, including both active processing time and downtime periods. Used for labor cost allocation and shift utilization analysis.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; Workday HCM — Labor Reporting

description: Externally-known business identifier for the sort session, used in operational reporting, shift logs, and AMCS platform references. Format: SS-YYYY-MM-DD-NNNN.
reference: AMCS Platform — Sort Line Operations; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Current lifecycle state of the sort session. 'active' indicates the session is in progress; 'completed' indicates normal closure; 'aborted' indicates premature termination due to equipment failure, safety event, or operational decision; 'paused' indicates a temporary halt; 'pending' indicates scheduled but not yet started.
reference: AMCS Platform — Sort Line Operations; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Classification of the sort session by operational purpose. 'standard' is a normal production run; 'trial' is a test run for new material streams; 'calibration' is a quality calibration run; 'training' is a supervised training session for new operators.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Classification of the work shift during which this sort session occurred. Used for labor cost allocation, productivity benchmarking across shifts, and workforce scheduling analysis.
reference: Workday HCM — Workforce Planning; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

business_glossary_term: Sort Line Belt Speed (Feet Per Minute)
description: Operational belt conveyor speed in feet per minute (FPM) at which the sort line was configured for this session. Affects throughput rate and operator sorting effectiveness. Used for equipment performance analysis.
reference: Infor EAM — Asset Lifecycle; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this sort session record originated. Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer. 'AMCS' indicates AMCS Platform; 'SAP' indicates SAP S/4HANA; 'MANUAL' indicates manual data entry.
reference: Waste Management Data Governance Standards; SOX Compliance — Data Lineage

description: The native identifier of this sort session record in the originating operational system (e.g., AMCS session ID, SAP production order number). Used for cross-system reconciliation and data lineage tracing in the Silver Layer.
reference: Waste Management Data Governance Standards; SOX Compliance — Data Lineage

description: Date and time when the sort session officially commenced, representing the principal real-world business event time. Used for throughput rate calculations, shift alignment, and operational KPI reporting.
reference: AMCS Platform — Sort Line Operations; SWANA MRF Operations Standards

description: Processing throughput rate measured in tons per hour (TPH) for this sort session. Calculated as input tonnage divided by active processing time. Key operational KPI for sort line efficiency and capacity planning.
reference: SWANA MRF Operations Standards; EPA Recycling Reporting Requirements

description: Timestamp when this sort session record was last modified. Used for change tracking, data reconciliation, and Silver Layer incremental processing.
reference: SOX Compliance — Audit Trail Requirements; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the service location (e.g., 'USA', 'CAN'). Supports international operations and regulatory compliance determination.

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this service address record originated (e.g., Salesforce CRM, Waste Logics, AMCS Platform, SAP S/4HANA). Used for data lineage tracking, conflict resolution during integration, and Silver Layer provenance auditing.

description: Indicates whether this service address is enrolled in a waste diversion program (recycling, composting, organics collection). Diversion Rate = percentage of waste diverted from landfill. reference: EPA Waste Diversion Reporting; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems; SWANA Diversion Rate Standards

description: Elevation of the service address above sea level in feet. Used for route planning in hilly or mountainous terrain to optimize vehicle fuel consumption and assess CNG (Compressed Natural Gas) vehicle suitability for the route.

description: The externally-known unique identifier for this service address as assigned by the source system of record (e.g., Waste Logics site ID, AMCS location code, or SAP SD ship-to party number). Used for cross-system reconciliation and integration.

description: Precision level of the latitude/longitude geocoding result for this service address. 'rooftop' indicates exact parcel-level match; 'range_interpolated' indicates interpolated from street range; 'approximate' indicates centroid-level. Drives confidence in route optimization and dispatch accuracy.
reference: Google Maps Geocoding API Standards; AMCS Platform Geocoding

description: Indicates whether this service address is designated for hazardous waste collection or handling services. When true, requires RCRA-compliant manifest tracking, specialized vehicle assignment, and Enviance EHS compliance workflows. Triggers additional regulatory reporting obligations.

description: Timestamp when this service address record was most recently updated, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver Layer pipeline and audit trail compliance.

reference: NWRA Container Sizing Standards; Waste Logics Container Management; AMCS Platform Container Tracking

reference: AMCS Platform Service Frequency Configuration; Waste Logics Service Scheduling; NWRA Service Standards

description: Business segment classification for the service address indicating the customer type served at this location. Aligns with B2C residential, B2B commercial, industrial, and government/municipal contract categories. Used for pricing, routing, and regulatory reporting.

Classification of the on-site hazardous waste accumulation area based on RCRA generator category and applicable time limits. LQGs may accumulate up to 90 days; SQGs up to 180 days (or 270 days in rural areas); VSQGs have no time limit but volume limits apply. Satellite areas are small accumulation points feeding a central accumulation area.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262 Subparts Aa, Bb, Cc; EPA Generator Improvements Rule

description: Due date for the next EPA Biennial Hazardous Waste Report submission. Required for LQGs in even-numbered years under RCRA 40 CFR Part 262.41. Tracks compliance calendar obligations for large quantity generators.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262.41; EPA Biennial Hazardous Waste Report

description: Indicates whether a RCRA-compliant emergency contingency plan is on file for this generator. LQGs are required to maintain a formal contingency plan under 40 CFR Part 262.261; SQGs must have an emergency plan. Critical for compliance verification and emergency response readiness.
Timestamp when this waste generator profile record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance record-keeping requirements under RCRA and SOX.
reference: SOX Section 404; RCRA Recordkeeping Requirements; ISO 14001

description: Indicates whether this generator is registered in the EPA's national e-Manifest system for electronic hazardous waste tracking. The e-Manifest system replaced paper manifests and is operated by the EPA under RCRA authority.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262 Subpart B; EPA e-Manifest (RCRAInfo)

description: Full name of the designated emergency coordinator responsible for implementing the contingency plan and coordinating emergency response at the generator site. Required to be listed in the contingency plan and available to local emergency responders under RCRA.

24-hour contact phone number for the designated emergency coordinator at the generator site. Must be posted at the facility and provided to local emergency response agencies as required under RCRA contingency plan regulations.

business_glossary_term: Estimated Hazardous Waste Volume (Kilograms per Month)
description: Estimated monthly generation quantity of RCRA-regulated hazardous waste in kilograms. This is the primary metric used to classify the generator into VSQG (≤100 kg), SQG (100–999 kg), or LQG (≥1,000 kg) categories and must be re-evaluated whenever operations change.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262.13; EPA Generator Improvements Rule

business_glossary_term: Estimated Monthly Waste Volume (Tons Per Day equivalent, monthly)
description: Estimated total waste generation volume per month expressed in short tons. Used to determine and validate RCRA generator category (VSQG/SQG/LQG), plan collection frequency, and support TPD (Tons Per Day) capacity planning for routing and disposal.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262.13; EPA Generator Category Thresholds

description: RCRA regulatory classification of the waste generator based on monthly hazardous waste generation quantity. LQG (Large Quantity Generator) generates ≥1,000 kg/month; SQG (Small Quantity Generator) generates 100–999 kg/month; VSQG (Very Small Quantity Generator) generates ≤100 kg/month. Determines applicable regulatory requirements, accumulation time limits, and manifest obligations.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262 Subpart A; EPA Generator Improvements Rule (2016)

description: Current lifecycle status of the waste generator regulatory profile. Active indicates the generator is currently producing regulated waste; inactive indicates operations have ceased; pending indicates initial registration is in progress; suspended indicates regulatory hold; closed indicates the site has been formally decommissioned.

Comma-delimited list of EPA hazardous waste codes (e.g., D001, F003, U080) applicable to the waste streams generated at this site as determined by TCLP (Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure) testing or listed waste classification. Required for manifest preparation and RCRA compliance reporting.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 261 Subparts C and D; EPA Hazardous Waste Codes

description: Outcome of the most recent regulatory inspection at this generator site. Significant violations may trigger enforcement actions, fines, or mandatory corrective measures under RCRA or CERCLA authority.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262; EPA RCRA Compliance Monitoring; CERCLA

description: Date on which the most recent EPA Biennial Hazardous Waste Report was submitted for this generator. Used to verify compliance with LQG biennial reporting obligations and to support audit documentation.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262.41; EPA Biennial Hazardous Waste Report

description: Date of the most recent regulatory compliance inspection conducted at this generator site by the EPA, state environmental agency, or Local Enforcement Agency (LEA). Used to track inspection history and assess compliance standing.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262; CERCLA; State Environmental Quality Departments; LEA

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this waste generator profile record in the data platform. Used for change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit trail maintenance.
reference: SOX Section 404; RCRA Recordkeeping Requirements; ISO 14001

description: Date of the most recent RCRA Site ID notification update submitted to the EPA or authorized state agency. Generators must re-notify when their generator category changes, when they begin generating new hazardous waste streams, or when site information changes.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262.18; EPA Generator Improvements Rule (2016)

description: Indicates whether this generator is required to use a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest (EPA Form 8700-22) for off-site shipments of hazardous waste. Mandatory for SQGs and LQGs; VSQGs are exempt from manifest requirements under 40 CFR Part 262.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262 Subpart B; EPA e-Manifest System

description: Maximum number of days this generator is permitted to accumulate hazardous waste on-site before it must be shipped to a TSDF, as determined by generator category and applicable RCRA regulations. Exceeding this limit triggers LQG-level requirements or potential RCRA violation.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262.17 (LQG); 40 CFR Part 262.16 (SQG); EPA Generator Improvements Rule

business_glossary_term: North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code
description: Six-digit NAICS code representing the primary industry classification of the waste-generating facility. Used by EPA and state agencies to categorize generator type, assess typical waste streams, and benchmark regulatory compliance requirements.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262; U.S. Census Bureau NAICS

description: Scheduled due date for the next required RCRA notification or re-notification. LQGs must notify every four years under the 2016 Generator Improvements Rule. Used by compliance teams to proactively manage regulatory deadlines.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262.18(d); EPA Generator Improvements Rule (2016)

description: Free-text field for compliance officers and environmental managers to record supplementary information about the generator's regulatory status, special handling requirements, enforcement history, or operational context not captured in structured fields.
reference: Enviance EHS; SAP S/4HANA EHS Module

description: Indicates whether this generator currently has one or more open, unresolved regulatory violations on record with the EPA or state environmental agency. Triggers enhanced compliance monitoring and may affect service agreements and manifest acceptance.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262; EPA Enforcement and Compliance Assurance; CERCLA

business_glossary_term: Personnel Hazardous Waste Training Current Flag
description: Indicates whether all relevant facility personnel have completed current RCRA hazardous waste management training as required for the generator's category. LQGs must provide formal classroom or on-the-job training; SQGs must ensure familiarity with emergency procedures.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Part 262.17(a)(7) (LQG); 40 CFR Part 262.16(b)(9) (SQG); OSHA 29 CFR 1910.120

description: The predominant category of waste generated at this site. MSW (Municipal Solid Waste) covers general commercial/residential refuse; C&D (Construction and Demolition Waste) covers building debris; hazardous covers RCRA-regulated hazardous waste; universal waste covers batteries, lamps, and pesticides; mixed indicates multiple co-dominant streams.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Parts 261–262; EPA Waste Classification Guidance

description: Date from which this waste generator regulatory profile is considered valid and active. Represents the start of the current regulatory classification period, which may be triggered by initial registration, a generator category change, or a site re-notification.

description: Maximum number of employees that can be assigned to this organizational unit based on operational requirements, facility capacity, or budget constraints. Used for workforce planning and resource allocation.

Soft delete indicator. True if this organizational unit record has been logically deleted but retained for historical reference, false for active records. Used for data retention and historical reporting.
Timestamp when this organizational unit record was last modified. Used for change tracking, data quality monitoring, and audit trail purposes.
Indicates whether this organizational unit operates on recognized company holidays. True for essential operations (e.g., landfills, emergency response), false for units that close on holidays.

Indicates whether this organizational unit operates on Saturdays and Sundays. True for units with weekend operations (e.g., collection routes, 24/7 facilities), false for standard Monday-Friday operations.
Standard daily end time for operations at this organizational unit in 24-hour HH:MM format. Used for shift scheduling, time and attendance rules, and operational planning.
Standard daily start time for operations at this organizational unit in 24-hour HH:MM format. Used for shift scheduling, time and attendance rules, and operational planning.

Current operational status of the organizational unit. Active units are fully operational, inactive units are temporarily non-operational, planned units are approved but not yet operational, closed units are permanently shut down, and suspended units are temporarily halted pending review.
Primary contact phone number for the organizational unit. Used for internal communication and employee contact.
ZIP or postal code for the organizational unit location. Supports geographic analysis and local regulatory compliance.

business_glossary_term: RCRA (Resource Conservation and Recovery Act) Permit Number
description: RCRA permit number for organizational units handling hazardous waste. Required for TSDF (Treatment Storage and Disposal Facility) operations. Null for units not handling hazardous waste.
reference: RCRA 40 CFR Parts 260-279 Hazardous Waste Regulations

description: OSHA-based safety risk classification for the organizational unit. Low risk for administrative offices, moderate risk for transfer stations, high risk for MRF and collection operations, hazardous for landfills and hazardous waste facilities. Determines PPE requirements, training protocols, and safety inspection frequency.

SAP FI/CO cost center code associated with this organizational unit for labor cost allocation, financial reporting, and budget tracking. Enables integration between workforce management and financial systems.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO Cost Center Accounting Standards

description: SAP FI/CO profit center code for revenue and profitability reporting at the organizational unit level. Used for P&L analysis and performance management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO Profit Center Accounting Standards

description: Two-letter state or province code where the organizational unit is primarily located. Used for state-level labor law compliance, tax reporting, and regulatory requirements.
IANA time zone identifier for the organizational unit location (e.g., America/New_York, America/Chicago). Used for shift scheduling, time and attendance, and cross-regional coordination.

Indicates whether employees in this organizational unit are represented by a labor union. True for unionized units, false for non-union units. Used for labor relations, collective bargaining, and compliance with union agreements.
reference: National Labor Relations Act (NLRA) Compliance Standards

description: Business identifier code for the organizational unit used across operational systems and reporting. Typically aligns with SAP organizational unit codes.
Full business name of the organizational unit (e.g., 'Northeast Region', 'Chicago MRF', 'Southern District').

Classification of the organizational unit within the hierarchy structure. Corporate represents headquarters, region covers geographic areas, district represents operational territories, facility includes MRF/landfill/transfer station/WTE plant locations, department covers functional groups, and cost center represents financial reporting units.
Unique identifier for this organizational unit in the Workday HCM system. Used for integration between lakehouse and source HCM system for employee assignments, payroll, and workforce planning.
